title: Title: Non-Euclidean Geometry for Cryptographic Key Distribution
abstract: The inherent unpredictability of cryptographic keys is a critical consideration in secure communication. Traditional key distribution methods are vulnerable to various attacks, necessitating the exploration of novel cryptographic paradigms. This paper proposes a novel cryptographic key distribution scheme predicated on non-Euclidean geometry, aiming to enhance security through inherent unpredictability. We detail the core mechanism – the generation and verification of keys through the manipulation of non-Euclidean geometric structures – and argue that this approach offers a fundamentally different and potentially more robust solution compared to existing methods. This work explores the mathematical foundations of this approach, including the geometric properties exploited for key generation, and discusses the potential implications for future cryptographic security. The focus is on demonstrating the effectiveness of this geometry-based approach through theoretical analysis and a preliminary investigation of its security properties.

title: Adaptive Reinforcement Learning-Based Dynamic System Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to dynamic system optimization utilizing adaptive reinforcement learning. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual design, limiting their applicability to complex systems. Our method adapts reinforcement learning algorithms to dynamically adjust optimization strategies, leading to enhanced efficiency and accuracy. We propose a framework that learns a state representation and dynamically adjusts the reward function, enabling the system to self-optimize and effectively address challenges in real-world dynamic environments. The core mechanism involves a continuous learning process driven by the reinforcement learning agent, ensuring adaptability and robustness to changing system conditions. This research explores the potential of this framework to significantly improve optimization performance across diverse system domains.

title: Adaptive Self-Mapping Algorithm for Dynamic Data Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Adaptive Self-Mapping Algorithm (ASMA) designed to dynamically model data distributions, leading to enhanced prediction accuracy. Traditional self-mapping techniques often rely on fixed parameter settings, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. ASMA employs a dynamic adjustment mechanism by iteratively adjusting key parameters, including mapping function parameters, iteration steps, and smoothing parameters, to optimize the algorithm's response to data variations. This approach allows for a more robust and accurate representation of complex data landscapes. The development of ASMA addresses the limitations of static self-mapping methods by providing a flexible framework for model refinement and improved predictive performance. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, discusses its performance evaluation through simulations, and presents a comprehensive analysis of its effectiveness in various data scenarios.

title: 基于自适应几何的量子电路的优化算法
abstract: Quantum computing is a rapidly evolving field with immense potential for scientific discovery and technological advancement. However, the development of efficient quantum circuits remains a significant challenge, demanding sophisticated optimization techniques. This paper proposes a novel optimization algorithm, termed "Adaptive Geometry Optimization" (AGO), that leverages the principles of self-adaptive geometry to dynamically adjust quantum circuit parameters, leading to improved performance. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the complex, non-linear nature of quantum circuits, while AGO offers a new approach to circuit design and optimization. The core mechanism of AGO involves systematically reshaping the circuit's geometry using a self-adaptive process, which results in enhanced circuit fidelity and ultimately, increased quantum computational capabilities. This research explores the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results of AGO, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve the performance of quantum algorithms.

title: Quantum Probability Perturbation Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum probability perturbation algorithm designed to optimize quantum system parameters and enhance quantum system performance. The algorithm leverages the principles of quantum superposition and entanglement to induce random perturbations within the system, facilitating a systematic search for optimal configurations. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, while this algorithm provides an automated approach to parameter refinement. The core mechanism involves manipulating quantum states through probabilistic interactions, ultimately leading to improved system performance. This work presents a framework for enhancing quantum system capabilities through intelligent parameter adjustments.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Time Complexity (D-AT) Algorithm
abstract: The Dynamic Adaptive Time Complexity (D-AT) algorithm presents a novel approach to optimization, specifically designed to address the challenges posed by large-scale problems. This algorithm dynamically adjusts the complexity of individual computation steps to optimize performance across a range of scenarios. The core mechanism revolves around intelligently reducing the computational burden through iterative complexity adjustments, resulting in significant improvements in efficiency. This paper explores the design and implementation of the D-AT algorithm, detailing its benefits, a rigorous analysis of its performance, and a comprehensive discussion of its potential applications across diverse optimization domains. We demonstrate its efficacy through a series of practical examples illustrating its ability to effectively tackle complex problems.

title: Neural Collective Behavior Modeling and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper explores the application of mathematical modeling and reinforcement learning to the study of neural network collective behavior. Traditional neural network optimization often relies on manual parameter tuning, limiting the model's adaptability. We propose a novel framework that integrates these approaches, simulating the collective learning process of neural networks using a mathematical model. This model leverages reinforcement learning to automatically optimize the network's parameters and enhance its generalization capabilities. The core mechanism involves mapping the neural network's collective behavior to a reinforcement learning environment, allowing the agent to iteratively improve the network's performance through trial and error. This approach offers a powerful and automated method for training neural networks, potentially surpassing traditional optimization techniques. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this combined approach in improving the robustness and generalization of neural network models.

title: Quantum-Inspired Memory Networks with Entangled Representation
abstract: Traditional memory networks (MemNets) face limitations in storing and retrieving vast amounts of sequential data efficiently. This paper proposes a novel architecture, Quantum-Inspired Memory Networks (QIMNs), designed to overcome these challenges by incorporating quantum-inspired entanglement between memory slots. The core idea is to mimic the principles of quantum entanglement to create a more compact and efficient representation of information within the memory network. This allows for faster retrieval and improved performance, particularly when dealing with long sequences. We introduce a mechanism that simulates entanglement, represented mathematically as a correlation function between memory slots. The network's architecture utilizes this correlation to reduce redundancy and accelerate information access. The proposed QIMN architecture is evaluated conceptually, outlining the key components and their interactions, and highlighting the potential benefits compared to conventional MemNets. We believe this approach offers a viable pathway for scaling memory networks to handle increasingly complex sequential data problems.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Statistical Inference – Leveraging Quantum Algorithms for Data Analysis
abstract: Quantum-enhanced statistical inference represents a significant advancement in data analysis, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to surpass the limitations of classical approaches. This paper investigates the design and implementation of a novel statistical inference algorithm, incorporating a quantum algorithm, designed to enhance accuracy and efficiency, particularly when dealing with large datasets. We explore the potential of quantum computation to accelerate computationally intensive tasks critical to statistical analysis, focusing on the application of a modified Grover's algorithm to estimate expected values. The core mechanism centers around exploiting quantum phenomena to reduce computational complexity and improve the reliability of statistical results. This work presents a comprehensive theoretical analysis and practical implementation demonstrating a substantial improvement over existing classical methods, particularly for large datasets, and lays the groundwork for a new paradigm in statistical data processing. The research culminates in a detailed discussion of the algorithm's performance characteristics and potential applications across diverse statistical domains.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Quantum State Simulation Validation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dynamic adaptive quantum state simulation to validate self-spin field simulations. Traditional self-spin field simulations often rely on pre-calculated parameters, limiting their accuracy. Dynamic adaptive quantum state simulation offers a novel approach by dynamically adjusting simulation parameters in real-time, thereby enhancing the verification process. We propose a method that continuously monitors and modifies the simulation, comparing the results against known experimental data to achieve robust validation. The core mechanism centers around a real-time parameter adjustment loop that iteratively refines the simulation state to minimize discrepancies. This approach addresses the limitations of static parameter settings, offering a more accurate and reliable validation method for self-spin field simulations. The resulting validation process allows for a more thorough investigation of the simulation's behavior and contributes to the development of improved self-spin field models. This work presents a framework for dynamic self-validation, offering a significant advancement in the verification of self-spin field simulations.

title: Bayesian Neural Network for Non-Stationary Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian neural network architecture designed to effectively model and adapt to non-stationary systems. Traditional neural networks often fail to handle dynamic environments due to their static parameterization. We propose a variational autoencoder-based approach that learns a latent representation of the system's dynamics, updating this representation during training via Bayesian inference. This allows for robust uncertainty quantification, enabling the model to better predict future states and handle changing conditions. The core mechanism centers around the variational autoencoder, which learns a compressed representation of the input data, enabling efficient Bayesian updates. We demonstrate the efficacy of this architecture through extensive experiments on a variety of non-stationary systems, showcasing improved performance and robustness compared to existing methods.

title: Evolve-CTF
abstract: This repository contains the complete research artefact for our study of agentic large language model (LLM) robustness using families of capture-the-flag (CTF) challenges. The study introduces Evolve-CTF, a framework for generating semantically equivalent challenge variants through controlled source-to-source transformations. These transformations preserve each challenge’s expected flag and underlying exploit strategy while modifying lexical or structural properties of the program. The repository includes: the source code of Evolve-CTF; the original and generated CTF challenge families; challenge variants produced using an external obfuscation tool; the complete run-level evaluation dataset; agent interaction traces and tool-use logs; processed data used to produce the reported results; statistical analysis scripts and model specifications; scripts and source data used to generate the tables and figures in the accompanying paper; and documentation for reproducing the transformations, evaluation, and analyses. The evaluation comprises 23,920 runs across 16 Python CTF challenges, 13 agentic LLM configurations derived from 9 base models, and 5 independent repetitions per evaluation condition. It examines challenge solvability, variation across challenge categories and LLM configurations, reasoning configurations, computational resource consumption, tool-use behaviour, and the additional effect of external obfuscation. This artefact is intended to support independent verification and reproduction of the reported findings, further analysis of the evaluation data, and future research on family-based robustness evaluation of tool-using LLM agents.

title: Bidirectional Influence of the Computational Modelling and Real-World: Theorising Coevolution of Agent-Based Models for Studying Energy Communities
abstract: This study hypothesises and explores the co-evolutionary patterns and potentially the bidirectional influence between computational modelling exercises and real-world practices by employing the elements of the co-evolutionary framework (i.e., technologies, formal institutions, user practices, business strategies and ecosystems) and focusing on the literature on the application of agent-based modelling and simulation (ABMS) for studying community energy systems (CESs). The study shows that modelling exercises are becoming more complex, including more elements and conditions from the real world. The results confirmed the co-evolutionary patterns and demonstrated that the evolution of technologies (e.g., from solar PV alone to multiple energy sources) and business strategies (e.g., peer-to-peer, real-time pricing and day-ahead market) is more significant than the other three elements. On the other hand, formal institutions and ecosystem elements received limited attention. The evolution of models of collective energy security is analysed as an example, further highlighting the evolution of technologies element. Given the detailed analysis of models developed to study CESs and the evolution of modelling practices, this study sheds light on the aspects and complexities that future studies should consider. The study and its findings contribute to strengthening modelling practices in the energy transition and, more broadly, in sustainability.

title: Privacy-preserving federated IoT intelligence for multimodal airway liberation decision support via offline reinforcement learning
abstract: Abstract Determining optimal timing for mechanical ventilation weaning remains a persistent clinical challenge, particularly in patients managed for upper airway pathologies—including post-operative head and neck surgery, laryngeal dysfunction, and obstructive airway conditions—where standard weaning criteria derived from general ICU populations may inadequately capture disease-specific physiological dynamics. We present an IoT-driven cyber-physical framework that continuously acquires and fuses four heterogeneous bedside data streams—ventilator waveform parameters, diaphragm ultrasound imaging features, arterial blood gas indices, and patient baseline profiles—within a gated recurrent architecture augmented by cross-modal attention. A Conservative Q-Learning agent learns a dynamic ventilation parameter adjustment policy from retrospective offline data, while a discrete-time survival model provides calibrated, uncertainty-aware individual weaning success probability estimates. To support privacy-preserving multi-center deployment across otolaryngology and head and neck surgery units, the framework employs a FedProx federated learning protocol with Gaussian differential privacy ($$\varepsilon = 1.0$$ ε=1.0) and MAML-style local personalization. Evaluated on 36,181 weaning episodes from MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD, the system achieves an AUROC of 0.893 on internal validation and 0.871 on external validation, with the federated variant narrowing the gap to centralized training to within 0.001 AUROC. These results demonstrate that integrating IoT-scale multimodal sensing with offline reinforcement learning and federated optimization yields a generalizable decision support system applicable to airway-complex patient populations encountered in otolaryngological practice. title: Optimizing Federated Learning Using Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) ensures data security and privacy, has become a viable decentralized method for training machine learning models across numerous clients without exchanging raw data. Conventional FL techniques, however, have drawbacks such expensive transmission, inconsistent client input, and ineffective model aggregation. To find these problems, the chapter proposes GNN-based optimization framework which improves the federated learning by detecting complications with client relationships. The methodology represents clients as graph nodes, with edges encoding pairwise similarities based on network proximity, model performance, and data distributions. During the model update phase, node embeddings that dynamically affect aggregation weights are learned using a Graph Neural Network (GNN). This technique mitigates the challenges posed by non-IID (non-independent and identically distributed) data in federated settings. This framework includes three primary mechanisms Graph Representation of clients, in which clients are showed as nodes in a graph with edges signifying model similarity. Graph convolutional networks is used to learn optimal weight assignments and refine global updates, which is represented as GNN-Based Aggregation and to transmit important chosen nodes which minimize the redundant updates can be optimized by Communication Optimization. The findings show the comparison of conventional FedAvg algorithm with FL techniques, the accuracy has increased 17%. Additionally it reduces communication overhead by 30% and increased the FLs scalability and efficiency by convergence value between 25–40%. This chapter presents the baselines in various scenarios and regulates the statistical variations effectively among clients. The evaluation results include GNNs with FL, which improves learning, performance, and resource efficiency.

title: NEAT-POCKET: Pocket-Conditioned Autoregressive 3D Molecular Generation with a Neighborhood-Guided Set Transformer
abstract: AI-driven de novo molecular design offers a promising route to accelerate early-stage drug discovery by generating novel ligands directly within target protein binding pockets. We present NEAT-POCKET, a pocket-conditioned extension of the autoregressive NEAT model for 3D molecular generation. NEAT-POCKET generates molecules atom by atom in protein pocket environments while preserving atom permutation invariance and explicitly modeling hydrogen atoms. Benchmarks on the CrossDocked and SPINDR datasets show that NEAT-POCKET achieves competitive structure-based generation performance while sampling substantially faster than existing baselines. Beyond full-molecule generation, NEAT-POCKET naturally enables pocket-conditioned fragment completion, a task directly relevant to lead optimization and scaffold elaboration. These results position NEAT-POCKET as a fast, flexible, and practical framework for structure-based drug design.

title: QUASAR: Quantum Satellite Architecture and Routing Simulator
abstract: The deployment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations is an important step toward global-scale quantum networking. However, evaluating satellite quantum network protocols under spatiotemporal orbital dynamics and quantum physical constraints remains computationally expensive and challenging. In this paper, we propose QUASAR, a lightweight simulator for evaluating entanglement distribution in satellite-based quantum networks. QUASAR provides a decoupled architecture that integrates dynamic orbital topologies, time-varying optical transmittance, and quantum memory decoherence into network- layer attributes. title: Long Horizon Transformer Quantile Fault Prediction for Multi Site Industrial Predictive Maintenance
abstract: Long-horizon predictive maintenance requires models to distinguish slowly evolving degradation from normal operating-regime variation over planning windows measured in days rather than hours. This paper evaluates whether an explicit conditional-quantile representation provides an informative classifier interface for this problem. The proposed TQRNN30d framework combines a dual-stage quantile regression neural network (QRNN) feature extractor with a multi-stream temporal fusion classifier. Each hourly word of 81-channel machine behaviour is mapped to a 324-dimensional quantile-state representation, and 720 ordered hourly words form the 30-day document supplied to the long-horizon model. The classifier fuses quantile states with dynamic covariates, channel-level static metadata, and a 168-hour latent-history stream using gated residual processing, causal recurrent encoding, and metadata-conditioned cross-modal attention. A bounded instability-aware signal derived from sustained one-word-ahead prediction-error divergence provides auxiliary memory modulation at the longest horizon. Evaluation uses a machine-disjoint 43/14/15 train/validation/test allocation across 72 machines in nine manufacturing facilities. At 30 days, TQRNN30d achieves 79.97% F1, 80.18% recall, 81.82% precision, 82.39% accuracy, and 0.820 ROC-AUC. It leads all 18 evaluated baselines at the 7-, 14-, and 30-day fixed-threshold comparisons, with the largest F1 advantage at 14 days. The results support held-out-machine performance within the observed homogeneous nine-facility fleet, but do not establish unseen-site, cross-equipment, or cross-sector generalisation.

title: Pixel-wise Planarity for High-Precision Monocular Plane Segmentation
abstract: Plane segmentation from a single RGB image remains challenging due to imprecise region grouping and geometrically inconsistent supervision, often leading to over-segmentation and false planar detections. We propose instead a pixel-wise planarity prediction framework for robust monocular plane segmentation. Building on a pretrained monocular geometric backbone predicting depth and surface normals, we introduce a dedicated planarity head that estimates per-pixel planarity confidence. During inference, predicted depth, normals, and planarity are combined in a lightweight region-growing procedure that enforces geometric consistency when forming plane segments. We further analyze existing plane ground-truth annotations and demonstrate substantial geometric inconsistencies under strict distance thresholds. Across multiple datasets, our method achieves improved geometric precision and segmentation quality compared to prior state-of-the-art approaches, while improving computational efficiency. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/alpayozkan/PixelwisePlanarity.

title: Compact-Memory LLM Agents via Online Max-Member Clustering and Atom-Aware Packing
abstract: Many long-horizon LLM deployments face tight prompt budgets: latency, cost, and context limits make full-context prompting impractical as interaction length grows. The key question is then not raw recall alone, but which memory design gives the best quality--token trade-off in the compact-memory regime. We present \textbf{RSM-full}, an online clustered-memory pipeline designed for a strong quality--token Pareto point. RSM-full combines two design choices: a cosine-gated \emph{max-member merge} write rule and an atom-aware grouped context packer. On AMA-Bench, our primary compact-memory benchmark, it reaches $83%$ of Full-Context quality at $32%$ of the token cost at a $4$k budget; under four-seed averaging it beats the closest streaming-clustered baseline (Online K-Means) by $+3.5$--$6.0$,pp ($p{<}.001$) across the whole ${\sim}2.6$k--${\sim}5$k regime. Three-seed ablations show most of this gain comes from the merge rule ($+5.7$,pp over Online K-Means and matched-$τ$ DP-means) and the grouped packer ($+5.0$,pp over flat concatenation). The pattern reproduces on RealMem, an independent long-horizon persona-memory benchmark: RSM-full improves on Budget-RAG ($+0.69$,pp, $p{=}.006$), is on par with BM25-RAG (paired $Δ{=}{+}0.27$,pp, $p{=}.47$; we do \emph{not} claim BM25 equivalence in the equivalence-test sense), and significantly outperforms Streaming-Proto ($+2.97$,pp) and the closest reproduced 2025 agentic-memory baseline A-MEM ($+1.65$,pp, $p{<}.001$). Across benchmarks the message is consistent: under tight budgets, compact-memory performance is driven mainly by how streaming memories are merged and how retrieved content is assembled. Overall, RSM-full is most useful when answeroughly $2k$--$5k$ prompt tokens, where itdefines a strong compact-memory Pareto point; higher-token baselines remain stronger outside this regime.

title: CAGE: Coherence-Aware Graph Encoding for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Traditional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems score each passage independently against the query, assembling context sets that may be individually relevant yet collectively incoherent. We introduce Coherence-Aware Graph Encoding (CAGE), a reranking framework that models "between-chunk coherence" across four dimensions: Intra-Domain Relevance, Noise Resistance, Informational Bonding, and Factual Consistency. Our pipeline transforms retrieved passages into directed heterogeneous entity graphs, amplifies factual anchors via min-out-degree reweighting, encodes structural patterns through a Relational Graph Convolutional Network, and fuses inter-chunk coherence with query relevance for final ranking. Evaluated across four multi-hop benchmarks, CAGE matches or outperforms strong baselines including monoT5 in Recall@5 on bridge-dominated datasets and consistently improves downstream Exact Match, demonstrating that structurally coherent context yields more precise answers even when retrieval recall is comparable or lower.

title: Anàlisi i caracterització experimental d'un sistema de distribució de parells de fotons entrellaçats
abstract: [EN] The project consists of the design, analysis, implementation, and characterization of an entangled photon pair distribution system between two terminal nodes. The design and analysis steps require the characterization of the entangled photon source (via the measurement of the entangled photon pair generation rate using photon counting methods, and the measurement of the polarization state density matrix of the source using quantum state tomography). Once the source has been characterized, the theoretical analysis of the entangled photon pair generation rate will predict the performance of the system operating through optical network infrastructure. The entanglement distribution scheme will be implemented, with at least one of the photons propagating through an optical fiber deployed in the Czech Technical University (CTU) building which connects two different laboratories. An assessment of the performance of the implemented setup will be executed, and the results will be compared with the theoretical predictions.

title: Probability Optimization Algorithm Evolution
abstract: Probability Optimization Algorithm Evolution (POAE) is a novel optimization algorithm designed to dynamically adapt to environmental changes, enabling long-term algorithm optimization and adaptation. This paper introduces a probabilistic framework where the algorithm's parameters are adjusted through a feedback loop based on observed environment dynamics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of POAE through simulations, showcasing its ability to maintain optimal performance across diverse scenarios. The core mechanism centers on a probabilistic neural network representing the algorithm's state, allowing for continuous learning and adaptation.

title: 基于量子纠缠的量子态预测的动态匹配
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state prediction method based on quantum entanglement, aiming to enhance prediction accuracy through dynamic matching of quantum states. We propose a technique that leverages the unique properties of entanglement to dynamically adjust the state of a quantum system, allowing for a more refined and accurate assessment of its future states. The core mechanism involves employing a controlled-phase evolution of the system's quantum state, guided by entanglement, to achieve a higher fidelity of state prediction. This approach offers a significant advancement in the field of quantum state estimation, potentially unlocking new capabilities in quantum information processing and analysis. The paper details the theoretical framework, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: ##混沌域的基于高频控制的非线性优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on the concept of a chaotic region, leveraging high-frequency control to extract optimal solutions and exhibit rapid adaptation to changing environments. The core mechanism involves simulating a system's dynamics within a chaotic region, generating feedback loops that guide the algorithm towards the optimum. The algorithm's effectiveness stems from its ability to identify and exploit the inherent unpredictability within the chaotic space, leading to significantly faster convergence compared to traditional optimization methods. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's performance in a complex, non-linear optimization problem.

title: Core Claim: Building a Quantum Computing Framework Based on Topological Structures, Utilizing Quantum Entanglement and Topological Properties, to Enhance the Efficiency of Quantum Algorithms and Expand Computational Capabilities, Particularly in Handling Complex Topological Data Structures.
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, but its practical application is hampered by limitations in algorithm efficiency and computational power, particularly when dealing with complex data structures. This paper introduces a novel quantum computing framework, the "Topological Quantum Computing Framework," predicated on the principles of quantum entanglement and topological properties. The framework aims to address these limitations by introducing a novel "Topological Quantum Entanglement" mechanism, which leverages topological properties to optimize quantum algorithm execution and improve the utilization of quantum entanglement. This approach offers a fundamentally new pathway towards enhanced efficiency and scalability in quantum computation, especially when applied to the analysis and manipulation of intricate topological data structures. The core mechanism centers around the creation and manipulation of topological quantum states, enabling novel quantum algorithms with significantly increased computational performance. We explore the potential of this framework for tackling complex problems and demonstrate its efficacy through illustrative examples. The research contributes to a deeper understanding of the intersection of quantum mechanics and computational complexity, paving the way for the development of more powerful and versatile quantum algorithms.

title: Dynamic Probability Field Models: Adaptive Feature Extraction Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probability field model-based feature extraction algorithm designed to automatically adjust feature extraction parameters, thereby enhancing feature extraction accuracy. Traditional feature extraction methods rely on manual parameter tuning, lacking the ability for automated optimization. The proposed algorithm utilizes a dynamic probability field as a core component, enabling adaptive parameter adjustment. This adaptive approach significantly improves the accuracy of feature extraction compared to conventional methods. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the probability field, which dynamically optimizes the feature extraction process. This results in a more robust and accurate feature representation. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, presents experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness, and concludes with a discussion of its potential applications.

title: 自适应量子态的概率生成算法
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, but its practical implementation faces significant challenges related to qubit stability and control. Quantum state generation is a critical step in quantum computation, and current approaches often rely on static strategies. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, "Quantum State Evolution and Adaptation" (QSEA), designed to address these limitations. QSEA dynamically adjusts the generation strategy based on predicted outcomes, optimizing quantum state generation for improved efficiency and accuracy. The core mechanism leverages a "Quantum State Evolution" process, iteratively refining the quantum state until a desired outcome is achieved. We present a comprehensive analysis of QSEA's performance across a range of quantum algorithms, demonstrating its potential to enhance quantum computing capabilities. This research contributes to the development of more robust and versatile quantum computation methodologies.

title: Non-Standard Metric Space Generation via Neural Network Auto-Mapping
abstract: This paper investigates the use of neural networks to generate novel metric spaces, aiming to improve the efficiency of optimization algorithms. Traditional metric space design often involves laborious manual creation, limiting the potential for discovering optimal configurations. We propose a novel approach that utilizes a neural network to automatically learn the structure of a metric space and dynamically generate new space based on the optimization process. The core mechanism involves a learning network that maps input data to a latent space, allowing for the generation of diverse and potentially higher-performing metric spaces. The paper details the design of a specific neural network architecture, its training procedure, and results demonstrating its effectiveness in generating novel space structures. The resulting system offers a new paradigm for metric space exploration, potentially accelerating the optimization process.

title: Dynamically Generated Modular Forms for Complexity Reduction
abstract: This paper investigates the use of dynamically generated modular forms as a tool for reducing the complexity of mathematical objects. The core concept is to design a system that generates modular forms, which are mathematical constructs that possess inherent structural properties, capable of iteratively simplifying a given object by strategically applying transformations. We propose a novel neural network architecture designed to learn the object's inherent structure and then generate a sequence of transformations that effectively 'undo' the object's complexity, creating a shortcut through a higher dimensional space. This approach offers a potential pathway for efficiently tackling computationally intensive problems related to geometric and algebraic objects. The paper details the neural network design, the transformation sequence generation process, and the resulting complexity reduction capabilities demonstrated through a simplified example.

We propose a novel neural network architecture designed to learn the object's inherent structure and then generate a sequence of transformations that effectively 'undo' the object's complexity, creating a shortcut through a higher dimensional space. This approach offers a potential pathway for efficiently tackling computationally intensive problems related to geometric and algebraic objects. The paper details the neural network design, the transformation sequence generation process, and the resulting complexity reduction capabilities demonstrated through a simplified example.

title: Bio-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithms for Network Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of bio-inspired evolutionary algorithms to the optimization of complex networks. Traditional network optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and scale of real-world networks, frequently relying on heuristics or gradient-based approaches with limited exploration capabilities. This research proposes a framework utilizing evolutionary algorithms—specifically, Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Neural Networks inspired optimization—to address these challenges. The core concept involves simulating evolutionary processes directly on network models, allowing for the systematic exploration of a vast solution space and the identification of configurations exhibiting desirable network properties. The methodology employs a population-based search strategy, mimicking natural selection, where individuals (network topologies) are evaluated based on a predefined fitness function, and successful individuals are used to generate new generations through crossover and mutation. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach, highlighting its potential for tackling diverse network optimization problems, including routing, topology design, and resource allocation. The results suggest that bio-inspired algorithms can significantly outperform traditional methods in terms of solution quality and convergence speed, particularly for complex, high-dimensional network optimization tasks. Furthermore, the framework is adaptable to various network types and optimization objectives, offering a versatile tool for network design and management.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology for Optimal Data Compression
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive topology for data compression, aiming to optimize for information content through dynamic topology adjustments. Traditional compression techniques often rely on fixed compression algorithms, failing to fully exploit the inherent structure of the data. We propose an algorithm that analyzes the data's structure and dynamically modifies the topology of data structures, creating a more efficient compression scheme. The core mechanism involves identifying patterns within the data and generating a topology that maximizes information density while maintaining compression efficiency. This approach offers a novel solution to the compression challenge, potentially significantly improving compression ratios compared to existing methods. The research explores the feasibility of this technique through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments, demonstrating its potential for achieving superior compression performance.

title: Phase-Shifted Quantum State Collapse (PSQC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum state collapse algorithm, Phase-Shifted Quantum State Reconstruction (PSQC), designed to improve the fidelity of quantum states, particularly in quantum simulations. The core innovation of PSQC lies in its utilization of phase-shifting to stabilize quantum states during collapse, mitigating the inherent instability and noise associated with traditional collapse methods. We detail the algorithm's architecture, demonstrate its efficacy through rigorous simulations, and discuss its potential impact on quantum information processing. The paper concludes with a comprehensive overview of the key concepts and future research directions.

This work demonstrates the potential of quantum entanglement to overcome limitations in traditional topological simulation methods, offering a fundamentally new pathway to advanced predictive modeling.

title: Matrix Probability Field
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Matrix Probability Fields (MPFs) as a novel framework for modeling and optimizing dynamic systems, specifically focusing on neural networks and chemical reaction dynamics. Traditional approaches often rely on precise mathematical equations, but MPFs offer a mechanism to represent and optimize system probabilities through probabilistic models. The core of this work centers around the construction of a matrix-based probability field, designed to facilitate efficient optimization and prediction within these complex systems. We present a mechanism for mapping variables to a matrix representation, leveraging the probabilistic nature of the field for optimization and predictive capabilities. The paper will detail the core mechanism, the significance of this approach, and the potential impact on various applications.

title: Probability Quantum Simulation of Multi-Particle Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic quantum simulation method designed to accurately model dynamic behavior of complex molecular and material systems, particularly those incorporating quantum effects and multi-body interactions. Traditional quantum simulation methods often suffer from computational limitations and struggle with the intricacies of multi-particle systems. This research introduces a method leveraging probabilistic logic to reduce simulation time and improve fidelity. The core mechanism involves integrating quantum mechanics with probabilistic logic to establish a robust and efficient representation of system states, thereby mitigating the challenges associated with complex simulations. The development of this approach offers a promising pathway to overcome existing limitations in quantum simulation, particularly for systems exhibiting quantum phenomena and intricate multi-body dynamics.

title: A PyTorch reimplementation of the Transformer Earthquake Alerting Model (TEAM)
abstract: A PyTorch reimplementation of the Transformer Earthquake Alerting Model (TEAM), a deep-learning method for earthquake early warning that predicts peak ground acceleration (PGA) probabilistically at arbitrary target coordinates. TEAM was introduced by Münchmeyer et al. (2021) in TensorFlow/Keras. The model takes the waveforms recorded so far by a seismic network and outputs, for every target location, a five-component Gaussian mixture over log₁₀(PGA). Exceedance probabilities for any threshold follow from that mixture, and a warning is issued the first time the probability crosses a decision level α. This repository also contains the training and evaluation pipeline used for a study of earthquake early warning on the Chilean subduction margin.

title: Разработка и исследование модели эффекта воздействия с учетом взаимосвязей между объектами
abstract: Настоящая работа посвящена разработке и исследованию модели трансформера с механизмом группового внимания для задач регрессии на табличных данных с групповой структурой. Предметом исследования являются методы и архитектуры моделей машинного обучения, использующие групповую структуру данных для повышения качества регрессионных предсказаний и оценки эффекта воздействия. Предложен механизм группового внимания, расширяющий стандартный multi-head attention за счёт аддитивной и мультипликативной модуляции весов внимания на основе матрицы групповых отношений. Матрица отношений строится локально для каждого батча на основе категориальных признаков, задающих групповую принадлежность объектов. Поддерживается несколько независимых каналов групповых отношений. Проведены эксперименты на синтетических и реальных наборах данных. Сравнение с трансформером без группового механизма и методами градиентного бустинга (XGBoost, CatBoost) показало, что предложенная модель превосходит конкурентов по метрике R^2 в большинстве рассмотренных конфигураций, демонстрируя особенно высокую устойчивость к шуму в признаках. На реальных данных с таксономической групповой структурой (Bird Genetic Diversity) трансформер с групповым вниманием достиг R^2 = 0.61 против 0.44 у градиентного бустинга. Дополнительно предложены два подхода к адаптации модели для задачи оценки условного среднего эффекта воздействия: двухэтапный, в котором T-learner формирует псевдо-аутком как начальное приближение CATE, а трансформер уточняет оценку используя индикатор воздействия в качестве группового канала механизма внимания, и двухголовая архитектура с двумя независимыми выходными слоями, обучаемая непосредственно на наблюдаемых исходах без вспомогательных моделей.

title: Robust Online Aero-Engine Blade Defect Detection via Dual-Alignment Test-Time Adaptation
abstract: Reliable visual inspection is essential for quality assurance in aero-engine blade manufacturing, where defect appearance may vary across production lines, imaging conditions, blade poses, and surface backgrounds. Such domain shifts cause a mismatch between training and deployment data and degrade the reliability of deep defect detectors in online inspection. This problem is particularly challenging because aero-engine blade images usually contain sparse defects, making pseudolabel-based adaptation vulnerable to noisy or missing predictions. To address this issue, we propose Aero-engine Blade Defect Detector (ABDD), an online adaptive detection framework based on test-time adaptation. ABDD introduces a Dual-Alignment Strategy to jointly adapt global visual style and local defect morphology by combining feature-statistics alignment with pseudo-box alignment. To reduce error accumulation from unreliable pseudo labels, an Uncertainty-aware Box Filtering mechanism evaluates pseudo boxes using classification confidence, classification entropy, and localization entropy. In addition, a lightweight Sparse Dilated Mona module enables parameter-efficient delta tuning while limiting source-domain forgetting. ABDD is evaluated on CD-AeBD and HD-AeBD under multiple domain-shift scenarios, with TTA strategies compared under a unified RT-DETR + Swin-T architecture. Experiments show that ABDD consistently improves detection robustness under domain shifts, and its practicality is further validated on an industrial inspection platform.

title: $N$-dimensional discrete Fourier transform via bosonic Hamiltonian
abstract: The discrete Fourier transform (DFT) underpins many classical algorithms and is a fundamental unitary operator for quantum information processing. Implementing the $N$-dimensional DFT in photonic integrated circuits (PICs) is limited by the cascades of Mach-Zehnder interferometers that current architectures require. Here we propose bosonic Hamiltonians that realize the $N$-dimensional DFT through a single stage of multimode evolution, complemented only by phase shifters before and after the interaction region, in a geometry suited to 3D waveguides. Modeling the system as a graph, where edges correspond to couplings and the vertices are the waveguides, we obtain analytical solutions for complete graphs up to $N=6$ and numerical solutions up to $N=31$. For non-complete graphs, different propagation constants are required in the Hamiltonian. We report all solutions for $N\leq 8$, partial exploration for $N=9$, and selected cases for $N=10$, together with three conjectures that guide the numerical search for $N \geq 11$. These configurations circumvent the vanishing evanescent coupling strength imposed by the waveguide separation, and a closed-form sensitivity criterion selects those that are admissible as a waveguide layout and least sensitive to fabrication error. We also uncover the missing non-affine parameters of the $6$-dimensional DFT, and show that the scaling law for implementing the $N$-dimensional DFT with our building blocks is $\mathcal{O}(N\log\log{N})$. This allows assembling the $2520$-dimensional DFT with only $2625$ interferometers, in contrast to the $\approx 3\times 10^6$ of Reck and Clements architectures.

title: ProCA: Progressive Contrastive Alignment for Robust EEG Visual Decoding
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) visual decoding aims to recover visual semantics from non-invasive neural time-series signals, for which robust alignment between noisy neural responses and stable semantic representations is key to achieving high-performance decoding. Despite recent advances in contrastive learning, robust EEG decoding remains challenging because existing methods rely on fixed visual or textual anchors whose semantic relations may become misaligned with EEG representations that vary across trials, subjects, and learning stages. Our empirical evidence shows that this instability appears across both standard EEG decoding protocols and more challenging robustness settings, including strict cross-subject transfer and realistic personalized continual adaptation. We provide a formal analysis showing that fixed semantic supervision can bias optimization when EEG-specific relations evolve, and that structure-agnostic perturbations may distort semantically important EEG components. To address these issues, we propose Progressive Contrastive Alignment (ProCA), a unified and model-agnostic framework for adaptive neural-semantic alignment. ProCA progressively refines class-level contrastive supervision from frozen vision-language priors to EEG-aware semantic relations, and introduces structure-consistent interpolation to constrain feature mixing according to channel-wise and temporal importance. Across subject-dependent, subject-independent, strict cross-subject transfer, and continual adaptation settings, ProCA achieves average relative Top-1/Top-5 gains of 7.4%/3.9%, 10.0%/4.6%, 28.1%/17.8%, and 16.8%/11.6%, respectively.

title: GNN-Guided Graph Coarsening and Adaptive QUBO Penalties for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows on a Quantum Annealer
abstract: Graph coarsening reduces the large Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) formulations arising when vehicle-routing problems are solved by quantum annealing. Nearby customers with compatible time windows are merged into super-nodes, the reduced problem is solved, and the solution is expanded to the original graph. For the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (CVRPTW), existing coarsening heuristics require family-specific tuning and remain unreliable on random instances. We address these limitations on the Solomon benchmark using simulated annealing and a D-Wave Advantage2 processor. We first introduce adaptive penalty calibration. Uniform penalty scaling has little effect, whereas controlling the internal coefficient range substantially improves raw samples. Removing non-binding constraints, normalising binding ones, and scaling the remaining penalties reduces mean raw constraint violations from 33.0 to 0.06 at the same solver budget (p=3.7e-11, n=56). A variable-count-preserving control attributes this gain to conditioning rather than problem size. Second, we replace the hand-tuned merge score with a graph neural network (GNN) using one configuration across all families. At N=10, it achieves 100% feasibility across all Solomon families, including R-type (100% vs. 80% for the tuned heuristic). Across N=10,...,100, feasibility is 83% vs. 69%, with the GNN better or tied on 85/90 instance-size pairs. At N=80,100, the difference is significant (p=0.002; 25/25 pairs), while the QUBO remains approximately 5-6 times smaller. Finally, hardware experiments reproduce the conditioning effect at fixed logical variable count: feasible samples increase from 0.02% to 39% across 13 instances. Classical repair with local search remains a reference bound for end-to-end solution cost.

Classical repair with local search remains a reference bound for end-to-end solution cost.

title: Translation Remainder Clause and Lean 4 Architecture
abstract: This repository contains the Translation Remainder Clause (TRC) v5 meta-analysis protocol and its accompanying machine-checked Lean 4 formal architecture. The TRC provides a domain-neutral audit grammar for tracking how information, uncertainty, boundary conditions, and alternative mechanisms are systematically discarded as observations move through institutional translation chains (Measurement → Raw Data → Processed Data → Consensus). The publication includes two primary components: 1. The Methodological Protocol and Cross-Domain Registry (TRC v5) A rigorously structured diagnostic methodology requiring an 8-field audit record for any consensus claim: the translation chain, the explicitly discarded remainder, a counterfactual relevance test, formal predicates, blocked obligations, a corrected scoped verdict, and a resolution condition. The document includes a 13-case exploratory registry demonstrating the framework's representational capacity across physics, biology, and computational domains. 2. Lean 4 Formal Architecture A machine-verified proof of the audit grammar's internal consistency, compiling with zero sorry placeholders and no non-standard axioms. The Lean 4 formalization enforces strict epistemic hygiene by: · Mandating Tier 0 Measurement Semantics: Empirical comparisons are restricted to tolerance-window overlap and band-disjointness, structurally forbidding the use of exact real-number equality for continuous measurements. · Treating Witnesses as Data: The architecture rejects Classical.arbitrary placeholders, forcing unmodeled remainders and blocked obligations to be carried as explicit, computable data within the type system. · Executing a Recursive Negative Control: The formalization includes a self-audit where the TRC protocol evaluates its own translation chain, mathematically proving that the framework's downgrade operations are idempotent and do not result in infinite regress or logical contradiction. Epistemic Scope and Boundary This artifact is an uncertainty-bearing research infrastructure, not a claim of universal physical law or institutional conspiracy. The Lean 4 formalization establishes the type correctness and formal coherence of the audit grammar; it does not establish the empirical adequacy of the underlying domain claims. The target quality of this methodology is remainder visibility: ensuring that the unverified boundaries of a scientific claim are explicitly carried forward into subsequent research.

title: Dynamic Variable Space Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic variable space optimization, designed to automatically adjust variable weights and distributions within a model to optimize its parameters and performance. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with dynamic environments, necessitating approaches that can adapt to evolving conditions. This work introduces a framework that leverages a dynamic variable space, allowing for continuous and adaptive parameter tuning. The core mechanism centers on the systematic adjustment of these variables, driven by a feedback loop that continuously evaluates model performance and refines the parameter set. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and qualitative analysis, showcasing significant improvements in model accuracy and efficiency compared to static optimization techniques.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology for Optimization – Quantum-Enhanced Topology Adjustment
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive topology for optimization, utilizing quantum entanglement to accelerate the convergence of optimization algorithms. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional spaces, necessitating computationally intensive search procedures. We introduce a novel technique that dynamically adjusts the topology of the problem space during optimization, leveraging quantum entanglement to create correlations between variables and enhance the evaluation of potential solutions. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of conventional methods by enabling a more holistic and flexible assessment of the search space. The core mechanism involves creating entangled pairs of variables, allowing for a more efficient exploration of the solution space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of simulations, showcasing significant improvements in convergence speed and solution quality compared to existing techniques. The potential implications of this research extend beyond optimization, potentially offering new insights into quantum information processing and computational geometry.

title: Title: Emergent Information Dynamics – Bayesian Inference with Adaptive Noise
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian inference framework centered on emergent information dynamics, specifically designed to effectively capture the complexity of systems exhibiting high-dimensional data. Traditional Bayesian methods often struggle with the inherent uncertainty of data, leading to suboptimal estimates. We propose a system that dynamically adjusts prior knowledge based on observed data, creating a more robust and accurate estimate through an adaptive noise process. This approach overcomes limitations of fixed prior distributions by incorporating a continuous refinement of the prior, enabling superior performance in challenging scenarios. The core mechanism involves a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) that continuously updates the prior distribution based on observed data, fostering a more efficient and reliable estimation process. This work explores how this adaptive approach mitigates the issues of over-fitting and under-fitting inherent in fixed prior models, offering a promising avenue for advanced statistical modeling.

title: Quantum Information Encoding for Complex Dynamical Systems
abstract: Quantum information encoding is a burgeoning field with the potential to revolutionize complex system modeling, particularly those exhibiting dynamic behavior. This paper investigates a novel approach to encoding complex dynamical systems into quantum information, leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve faster and more precise simulation compared to classical methods. We propose a method centered around the creation of entangled states that directly represent the state space of the system, offering a significant advancement in the ability to efficiently simulate and control these intricate systems. The core mechanism hinges on exploiting the inherent correlations within entangled states to facilitate a more streamlined and accurate representation of the system's dynamics. The potential impact of this research extends to diverse areas, including control systems, optimization, and fundamental physics research.

The core mechanism of this framework involves introducing a self-organizing quantum algorithm that dynamically allocates and optimizes quantum resources based on inherent quantum properties. We demonstrate the framework's potential to significantly enhance the efficiency and scalability of quantum computations through automated resource management. This research explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of the SQA framework, highlighting its advantages in achieving efficient quantum computation.

abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, particularly in complex data analysis and optimization. Traditional machine learning approaches often struggle to effectively handle data variations and complex relationships. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

abstract: This paper investigates a novel dynamic algorithm for topology transformation, leveraging adaptive topology transformation evolution. Traditional approaches often employ fixed transformation strategies, potentially offering suboptimal performance in dynamic scenarios. We propose a mechanism, the "Dynamic Topology Transformation Evolution," that dynamically adjusts the transformation strategy based on the topology's evolving characteristics. title: Title: Predictive Geometry with Adaptive Topology
abstract: Predictive Geometry with Adaptive Topology presents a novel approach to geometric prediction, moving beyond static topology models. The system leverages a self-organizing neural network trained to analyze geometric properties and dynamically adjust topology during prediction, resulting in more robust and adaptable geometric representations. This research addresses the limitations of traditional methods by incorporating a continuous refinement process, offering a significant advancement in predictive geometry. We detail the core mechanism of the neural network, its training process, and the resulting predictive capabilities. The system's ability to learn and adapt the topology of a mathematical object directly from its geometric characteristics promises to yield improved accuracy and flexibility compared to existing approaches. This work explores the potential of iterative refinement and self-organization to create a system capable of capturing complex geometric relationships with high precision.

title: Quantum Random Field-Based Simulated Evolution Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to accelerating the convergence of Simulated Evolution Algorithms (SEA) by leveraging the inherent randomness of Quantum Random Fields (QRFs). The core idea is to utilize QRFs as a dynamically generated search space for SEAs. QRFs, characterized by their unpredictable and non-deterministic nature, offer a significantly higher degree of exploration compared to traditional, deterministic search spaces. This allows the SEA to escape local optima more effectively and converge towards global optimal solutions faster. The proposed method is evaluated theoretically and presented as a framework for future research. We demonstrate the potential for significant performance improvements when applied to various optimization problems. The algorithm is designed to be adaptable to different problem landscapes and SEA parameters. Further research will focus on refining the integration process and exploring the theoretical underpinnings of this approach.

title: Self-Referential Quantum Circuits for Universal Computation
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum computation centered around self-referential quantum circuits. The core concept involves designing circuits that recursively incorporate themselves into their operational structure, effectively creating computational modules capable of self-replication. This is achieved through the strategic implementation of feedback loops and entanglement within the circuit architecture. The potential benefits of this paradigm include a reduction in circuit complexity and the possibility of constructing universal quantum computers from fundamentally simpler components. The theoretical framework presented herein outlines the key principles and mathematical underpinnings of this self-referential design, proposing a pathway toward more efficient and scalable quantum computation. The presented model uses the following notation: |ψ⟩ represents a quantum state, U(θ) represents a unitary operator with rotation angle θ, C represents a quantum circuit, and E represents the expectation value. Specifically, the expectation value of an observable A is denoted as E[A] = <ψ|A|ψ>, where |ψ> is the quantum state. The Hamiltonian of a quantum system is typically represented as H, and the time evolution of the state is governed by the Schrödinger equation: iℏ∂|ψ(t)⟩/∂t = H|ψ(t)⟩. Entanglement is represented by the Bell state |Φ⁺⟩ = (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2. Quantum gates, such as the Hadamard gate (H) and the CNOT gate (CN), are represented as unitary transformations. The circuit representation involves sequential application of gates, and the overall unitary transformation is the product of these gates. The circuit depth, denoted as d, represents the number of consecutive gate operations applied to a quantum state. The circuit complexity, denoted as C, is a measure of the number of gates required to implement a specific quantum algorithm. The circuit fidelity, denoted as F, quantifies the accuracy of a quantum circuit's output, ranging from 0 to 1. We define the quantum state preparation as |ψ⟩ = ∑i ci|i⟩, where ci are complex coefficients and |i⟩ are the computational basis states. The unitary transformation is defined as U|ψ⟩ = ∑i (Uici)|i⟩, where Ui are the matrix elements of the unitary operator U. The propagation of quantum states through a circuit is represented by the Schrödinger equation, and the final state is obtained by applying the unitary transformation to the initial state. The concept of quantum coherence, denoted as χ, represents the ability of a quantum system to maintain its superposition state. The fidelity of a quantum state is defined as the probability that a measurement will yield the expected outcome.

title: Title: Automated Proof Synthesis via Probabilistic Reasoning
abstract: Automated proof synthesis is a challenging yet increasingly important area in mathematics. This paper explores a novel approach to this problem—a system leveraging probabilistic reasoning and formal induction to automatically generate proofs for mathematical theorems. We propose a system that constructs intermediate steps in the proof process, focusing on generating properties rather than complete theorems, to reduce manual effort and potentially improve the efficiency of mathematical discovery. The core mechanism involves utilizing probabilistic models to guide the proof generation, enabling automated verification and refinement. This work addresses the limitations of current methods by automating a crucial and time-consuming step in mathematical reasoning. The system will be evaluated against a benchmark set of mathematical theorems to demonstrate its effectiveness and potential impact.

title: Interpretability for Turing Machines: data and code
abstract: Data and code behind the paper Interpretability for Turing Machines (Snikkers, Salazar, Murfet, Troiani). The experiments study the solution set of a fixed decision task (accept a short string iff it contains an A or a 0) realised as 38,019 canonical deterministic finite automata (DFAs), and probe their loss landscape with susceptibilities. The archive contains: the experiment runs as Zarr v3 stores: susceptibility matrices, embeddings, rank statistics and labels for all 38,019 canonical solutions the five running examples M1–M5 a 35-temperature sweep the GRLD/NUTS sampler-convergence runs the analysis library that computes susceptibilities, block ranks, and symmetries the implementation of noisy Turing machines and samplers (GRLD, NUTS, and the smooth relaxation) Files are path-preserving zips: code.zip unpacks to code/, experiments.zip to experiments/ (everything except the temperature slices), and each temperature_sweep_slice_beta*.zip holds the susceptibility slice at one inverse temperature, unpacking into experiments/temperature_sweep/susceptibility_slices/. Unzipping them all in one directory reconstructs the full layout, so you can download only the parts you need. A top-level README documents the layout, gives a loader, and includes a data dictionary mapping array names to the paper's notation. An interactive visualisation of the embedding data can be viewed at https://tminterp.timaeus.co

The archive contains: the experiment runs as Zarr v3 stores: susceptibility matrices, embeddings, rank statistics and labels for all 38,019 canonical solutions the five running examples M1–M5 a 35-temperature sweep the GRLD/NUTS sampler-convergence runs the analysis library that computes susceptibilities, block ranks, and symmetries the implementation of noisy Turing machines and samplers (GRLD, NUTS, and the smooth relaxation) Files are path-preserving zips: code.zip unpacks to code/, experiments.zip to experiments/ (everything except the temperature slices), and each temperature_sweep_slice_beta*.zip holds the susceptibility slice at one inverse temperature, unpacking into experiments/temperature_sweep/susceptibility_slices/. Unzipping them all in one directory reconstructs the full layout, so you can download only the parts you need. A top-level README documents the layout, gives a loader, and includes a data dictionary mapping array names to the paper's notation. An interactive visualisation of the embedding data can be viewed at https://tminterp.timaeus.co

title: Neuromorphic Computing in Sports
abstract: Brain-inspired AI and neuromorphic computing are changing the world of sports technology by making training, performance tracking, and injury prevention smarter and faster. These advanced AI systems function similarly to the human brain, enabling the creation of wearable devices, innovative training tools, and AI-based recovery systems for athletes. This chapter explores how brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), AI-powered coaching tools, and innovative sports gear can improve reaction time, monitor fatigue, and even facilitate injury recovery. From high-tech fitness wearables to AI-driven rehabilitation and virtual reality (VR) training, neuromorphic computing is enhancing sports technology to make it more intelligent, efficient, and personalized for athletes. The chapter also examines future innovations, such as real-time movement tracking, AI-driven biomechanics, and innovative sports gear, that can help athletes train more effectively and reduce the risk of injury.

title: Strong-Drive Limits in Josephson Circuits: From Chaos to an Unbound-Resonance Threshold
abstract: Strong microwave drives enable fast measurement and parametric control in superconducting circuits but can induce transitions out of the intended low-energy manifold. We develop a unified description of strong-drive limits in flux- and charge-driven Josephson circuits across drive frequency and dc flux bias. Using classical phase-space analysis and Floquet--Markov simulations, we identify distinct low- and high-frequency mechanisms. At low frequency, we characterize bound-state resonances and separatrix chaos and find that the flux-drive chaos threshold depends strongly on dc flux bias. At high frequency, these mechanisms are suppressed, and the dissipative steady state transfers from the central bound-state sector to outer resonances formed by above-barrier running trajectories. The resulting unbound-resonance threshold is nearly independent of drive frequency and circuit parameters over the regime studied and is controlled primarily by dc flux bias. Coherent simulations show that parametric operation persists beyond this threshold, but at a reduced rate, setting an effective upper bound on the achievable operation speed. We derive analytical criteria for both thresholds, validate them numerically, and experimentally confirm the predicted dc-bias dependence of the low-frequency threshold in a flux-driven SQUID. We also determine the timescales for transfer into the unbound-resonance regime and relaxation back to the bound-state manifold after the drive is removed. Finally, we relate the stability limits to a complementary picture based on the junction critical current and extend the framework to multitone drives and inductively shunted circuits. Together, these results identify the mechanisms limiting strong driving and suggest routes to extend the stable operating range of Josephson circuits.

title: Mitigating Performance Discrepancy in Cross-Domain 3D Class-Incremental Learning
abstract: 3D perception plays a crucial role in real-world applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, and AR/VR. In practical scenarios, 3D perception models need to continually adapt to newly emerging 3D object categories, making class-incremental learning (CIL) particularly important. However, unlike 2D images, 3D point clouds are inherently heterogeneous: objects from the same class may not only come from the clean CAD domain, but also from RGB-D camera scans of varying quality, video reconstructions, or even corrupted observations. We discover that such heterogeneity introduces a new challenge beyond catastrophic forgetting: the degree of performance degradation can vary substantially across domains, a phenomenon we term performance discrepancy. To investigate this problem, we establish the Domain3D-CIL training and evaluation protocol, which contains point cloud categories from heterogeneous domains. We further adapt a wide range of mainstream CIL methods to the 3D modality. The results demonstrate that this performance discrepancy consistently appears across these baselines. To mitigate this issue, we introduce PolyMem, an exemplar-free approach that implicitly models rich high-order statistics of the feature distribution to enhance cross-domain robustness. Experiments demonstrate that our method effectively alleviates the performance discrepancy while improving the model's performance across domains. Code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

title: Statistical Inference for Adversarial Training: Central Limit Theorems via Optimal Transport
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to rigorously quantify the statistical and learning-theoretic properties of adversarial training models for classification. Equivalently, we establish the statistical properties of empirical optimal partial transport. Precisely, first we provide two types of central limit theorems (CLT): CLT centered at the expected empirical value, and CLT centered at the population one with smoothing. These results are based on the uniqueness of optimal potential for various equivalent optimal transport formulations, and the empirical process theory argument. For the binary setting, we indeed prove the uniqueness of optimal potential by leveraging the connection between optimal partial transport and the derived multi-marginal optimal transport formula. As byproducts, we also obtain the stability of a saddle point of the adversarial training model, and the sample complexity and concentration probability of the generalization error.

title: $τ^τ$-Bench: An Environment for End-To-End, Realistic Agent Construction
abstract: LLM agents are rapidly becoming production software, deployed to handle customer service, adjudicate disputes, and operate internal systems. Notably, the work of building them is increasingly handed to coding agents, yet existing benchmarks say little about whether an AI system can deliver one under the conditions of a real client engagement. We introduce $τ^τ$-bench (pronounced hyper-tau-bench), a benchmark that makes agent construction the task. A developer agent is given the records a business actually keeps, a client who holds requirements, a production API that operations must run through, a codebase to inherit, and limits on serving cost and models: the same starting point a real engagement provides. From these it must deliver a complete customer-service agent, scored by deploying that agent against held-out simulated users. Across 53 tasks spanning four domains, the strongest configuration, Claude Opus 5 under Claude Code, passes just 23.9% of evaluation simulations. Meanwhile, an expert-authored reference ceiling scores 82.2%. The failures mirror ones human agent developers see: models issue shallow queries in place of deep comprehension of the records, communicate almost nothing to the client, and experiment too little with agent architecture and serving spend, shipping the first design that runs. We aim for $τ^τ$-bench to turn the work of cooperative agent building into a measurable target for coding agents.

title: CHAMP: Cross-domain Hybrid Architecture for Matchmaking and Prediction in Online Multi-Player Games
abstract: Multiplayer Online Battle Arena (MOBA) games rely on matchmaking to maintain competitive balance. Our prior work, CUPID, framed matchmaking as an assignment re-optimization problem and showed that a single-mode win-rate predictor can meaningfully rebalance teams. However, deploying such a system across diverse player populations exposes three practical bottlenecks: most queueing players lack sufficient in-mode match history (cold start), skill distributions shift drastically across rank tiers (distribution inconsistency), and extreme skill segments are severely data-starved. We present CHAMP, a cross-domain matchmaking framework that resolves these deployment bottlenecks. To address data sparsity and cold starts, CHAMP replaces the target-mode-only player profile with a hybrid domain feature collection: a timestamp-ordered cross-mode short-term sequence whose slices are annotated with target-domain features, plus per-mode breakdowns of long-term, real-time and team statistics. We further propose the Domain-Aware Win-rate Network (DAWN): a Domain-aware Knowledge Extractor (DAKE) compiles target-mode attributes into learnable representations that feed Domain-Aware Temporal/Spatial/Permutation OmniNet Encoders (DATOE/DASOE/DAPOE), so that mode-conditioned representations and per-mode debiasing are learned jointly inside a single shared network. Online, one trained DAWN serves every supported mode, with per-mode position-satisfaction thresholds as the only mode-specific knob. Offline, DAWN achieves 67.73% win-rate prediction accuracy, outperforming all evaluated attention and sequence baselines. Online A/B tests across the entire League ladder of a large-scale MOBA game, from novice players up to the top-expert players served by Elite Mode, demonstrate consistent drops in imbalanced matches. For lower-tier players, CHAMP reduces the 5-minute kill crushing rate by up to 20.73%.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Decoding for Improving Truthfulness in Open-Ended Generation
abstract: Ensuring truthfulness in large language models remains a critical challenge for reliable text generation. While supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with human feedback have shown promise, they require substantial amount of annotated data and computational resources, limiting scalability. In contrast, decoding-time interventions offer lightweight alternatives without model retraining. However, existing decoding strategies often face issues like prompt sensitivity, limited generalization, or dependence on internal model states. We propose a context-aware adaptive decoding method that leverages a compact reference grounding space, built from as few as 10 annotated examples and comprising pairs of context embeddings and next token logits from truthful responses, to enable retrieval-based logit shaping during inference. At each decoding step, our method retrieves top-N semantically similar contexts and aggregates their associated next token logits to modify the LLM's logits. Across three open-ended question-answering benchmarks, our approach achieves a 2.8 percent average improvement on TruthfulQA and further outperforms existing baselines on both Biographies and WikiQA. Experimental results also demonstrate cross-task generalization, with TruthfulQA-derived grounding enhancing biography generation. Our model-agnostic, scalable, and efficient method requires only a single generation pass, highlighting the potential of context-aware decoding for factual reliability in LLMs.
