title: ConsensusBench: Benchmark of Consensus Nodes for LLM Reasoning via Outcome Reward Densifying
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become one of the primary paradigms for reasoning enhancement of large language models (LLMs). In particular, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and related algorithms have demonstrated strong performance with outcome-level rewards. However, these methods depend solely on the final answer, without feedback regarding which intermediate steps contribute to success or failure. As task complexity and reasoning trajectory length increase, such sparse final-answer rewards become increasingly insufficient. To address this limitation, we introduce ConsensusBench, a novel dataset designed to provide rule-based process-level signals. We posit that a correct final answer relies on a small set of intermediate conclusions throughout the reasoning process, which can be seen as a verifiable sub-outcome. We identify these sub-outcomes by filtering correct trajectories from N rollouts and clustering semantically equivalent intermediate statements. We call these clustered statements as Consensus Nodes. By integrating a rule-based process reward derived from these nodes into GRPO-style algorithms, we develop a new reinforcement learning signal named ConsensusPR. It directly reduces the reward sparsity of outcome reward across long reasoning trajectories. To facilitate systematic process-level evaluation, we introduce three metrics to our benchmark: Final Answer Accuracy (Acc), Node Coverage Rate (NCR), and Tokens per Node (TPN). Experiments across AIME 2024, AIME 2025, GSM8K, MATH-500, and our ConsensusBench demonstrate that the proposed method consistently surpasses GRPO-style approaches, highlighting the practical value of consensus nodes in guiding reasoning.

title: Beyond Prompts: Measuring and Optimizing LLM Tool-Agent Harnesses
abstract: LLM tool agents can be improved without retraining by modifying the runtime harness around a fixed model: prompts, tool interfaces, middleware, state handling, and recovery logic. We study this setting as resource-bounded harness selection for fixed-model multi-turn tool agents, with the search surface scoped to prompts and tool-boundary middleware: edits are guarded intercepts at the tool boundary, not arbitrary rewriting of agent execution logic. Our optimizer-agnostic protocol reports mean held-out lift, worst-condition lift, repeatability, logged cost diagnostics, and RelLift95(B), a conservative estimate of the held-out gain of the harness selected under budget B. We instantiate the protocol with prompt-only and prompt-plus-middleware optimizers, including PRISM, which clusters failures and routes repairs to prompt, tool-boundary middleware, or joint edit surfaces within a Pareto search. On BFCL multi-round, tau2-Retail, and tau2-Telecom, PRISM obtains mean held-out lifts of 14.2, 14.9, and 10.1 percentage points and positive empirical RelLift95 on all three benchmarks, and a component ablation attributes the margin chiefly to failure-surface routing and the edit-pattern constraint. Across optimizers, the results show that some search procedures can occasionally find large gains but still choose brittle updates, so the reliability of the chosen harness should be reported alongside average held-out lift.

On BFCL multi-round, tau2-Retail, and tau2-Telecom, PRISM obtains mean held-out lifts of 14.2, 14.9, and 10.1 percentage points and positive empirical RelLift95 on all three benchmarks, and a component ablation attributes the margin chiefly to failure-surface routing and the edit-pattern constraint. Across optimizers, the results show that some search procedures can occasionally find large gains but still choose brittle updates, so the reliability of the chosen harness should be reported alongside average held-out lift.

title: MedWER: A Reproducible, Model-Free Evaluation Protocol for Medical Speech Recognition
abstract: Overall word error rate hides clinically critical errors: a transcript can be 95% correct and still swap one drug for another. The usual fix weights errors on medical entities, and almost always depends on an evaluation-time named-entity recognition (NER) model or cloud API, which makes the metric's denominator a versioned black box. We present MedWER, an evaluation protocol and open-source tool for medical ASR whose denominator is a fixed, license-clean term list: 19,373 drug, diagnosis, symptom, and injury-mechanism entries projected from public sources. The protocol couples a pinned text normalizer with a phrase-aware term-restricted WER, the MedWER, so the only versioned component is a normalizer dependency held at an exact release and checked against committed golden fixtures. Coverage is validated against an independent provincial drug-benefit file the list was not built from; the matching heuristic is calibrated against ground-truth entity spans. Baselines for Moonshine~base, Whisper~base.en, and MedASR on two open benchmarks are scored with the released tool and reported with 95% confidence intervals from resampled per-utterance scores.

title: MiDShip: Multimodal Dataset of Ship Cargo Hold Structures for Engineering Design
abstract: Ship structures govern vessel strength, safety, and manufacturability, but their design must satisfy hundreds of classification society requirements, making the process complex and iterative. Data-driven approaches are limited by the lack of structured datasets linking design geometry, structural performance, and rule-based constraints. This paper presents MiDShip, a multimodal dataset of 12,753 synthetic cargo-hold structural designs: 6,020 random, 496 generated by an SGLD-inspired procedure, and 6,237 generated by an equation-informed repair procedure. Each design includes parametric data, full and mesh-ready 3D geometry, engineering drawings and annotations, a bill of materials, and preliminary structural evaluations. Twenty-five constraints derived from a subset of ABS MVR are also evaluated. None of the random designs satisfies all constraints. Among the SGLD-inspired designs, 322 (64.9%) were fully compliant, with an average of 0.409 violations, 82.7% below the seed mean and 96.9% below the random-design mean. The repair procedure, developed through LLM-assisted code analysis, produced 4,952 fully compliant designs (79.4%), averaging 0.296 violations, 97.1% below the paired-source mean. In equal-size comparisons, mean nearest-neighbor distances in the scaled 120-parameter space were 3.495 for repaired designs, 1.144 for SGLD batches, and 3.729 for random designs. The primary contribution is the synchronized dataset and its generation and evaluation infrastructure; the generation studies demonstrate its utility rather than proposing new optimization algorithms. MiDShip supports machine learning, generative design, and automated rule-based evaluation for ship structures.

title: Reproducibility Package for "Disentangling Decoder Capacity and Directionality in Type Constrained Knowledge Graph Link Prediction"
abstract: This record provides the data, code, derived results, frozen configurations, and reproducibility materials supporting the article "Disentangling decoder capacity and directionality in type constrained knowledge graph link prediction," in Discover Computing (2026), DOI: 10.1007/s10791-026-10545-8.The package contains redistribution-permitted derived graph data, including anonymized node and edge lists, node features, graph and split manifests; implementations of the shared inner-product (IP), relation-specific diagonal (RD), symmetric bilinear (SB), and directed bilinear (D) decoders; frozen configurations for the matched 3 × 4 × 10 = 120-cell GCN/GraphSAGE/GAT study; seed-level and summary results; fixed-negative and full filtered-ranking outputs; deterministic semantic hard-negative pools, eligibility manifests, and evaluation outputs; paired statistical analyses; a threshold-free candidate queue; frozen-embedding symmetric/skew diagnostics; auxiliary five-seed and external-benchmark artifacts; tests; a minimal execution example; exact verification commands; and file-level SHA-256 hashes.The confirmatory 120-cell analysis is kept separate from auxiliary experiments. Official CMSR and CSDV source documents and verbatim regulated text are not redistributed. The ogbl-biokg benchmark is available separately through the Open Graph Benchmark. Code is licensed under the MIT License; redistribution-permitted derived data, result tables, and figures are licensed under CC BY 4.0.

title: Adaptive Quantum Error Correction via Dynamic Phase Folding
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for breakthroughs across diverse fields, but the inherent fragility of quantum states necessitates robust error correction techniques. Traditional methods often rely on computationally intensive decoding processes, limiting scalability and reliability. This paper introduces an innovative adaptive quantum error correction protocol, termed Dynamic Phase Folding, designed to minimize the impact of errors by dynamically adjusting the quantum state based on real-time error rate monitoring. We detail the core mechanism involving a self-organizing phase folding scheme, coupled with a sophisticated feedback loop to optimize the correction process. The proposed protocol demonstrates significant improvements in error correction rates and resilience compared to existing methods, offering a pathway towards practical and reliable quantum computation.

title: Non-Linear Chaos Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on non-linear chaos theory, specifically designed to adapt to dynamic system perturbations. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with non-stationary problems and lack the ability to dynamically adjust parameters in response to subtle changes. Our proposed algorithm, dubbed "Dynamic Chaos Adaptation" (DCA), employs a feedback mechanism inspired by chaotic dynamics to continuously refine the optimization objective based on the system's inherent fluctuations. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of simulations, showcasing its superior performance compared to established optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios involving complex, non-linear systems. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a dynamic relationship between the optimization target and the underlying chaos, enabling the algorithm to proactively address system instability.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum Computing Model Validation
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for quantum computing model validation based on dynamic topology. The core idea is to leverage the inherent properties of dynamic topology to rigorously verify the correctness and efficiency of quantum algorithms, enhancing the reliability and performance of quantum computation. We explore the application of this framework to quantum information and quantum cryptography, demonstrating its potential to improve the robustness of these critical areas. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum algorithms and provides a new approach to validating the complex and sensitive nature of quantum systems.

title: Title: Dynamic Matrix Optimization for Feature Selection in Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores a novel dynamic matrix optimization algorithm designed to enhance feature selection within machine learning models. Traditional feature selection methods often lack the adaptability necessary to effectively capture the nuances of evolving data distributions during model training. The proposed algorithm leverages a dynamic matrix representation of the feature space, adjusting feature weights based on real-time performance metrics derived from the learning process. The core mechanism centers on a learning process that dynamically adjusts the feature selection weights, ultimately improving model accuracy and generalization ability. The algorithm's ability to adapt to changing data characteristics offers a significant advancement in feature selection techniques, particularly within the context of complex machine learning models.

abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum algorithms to enhance fractal dimension estimation, focusing on the innovative application of wave function collapse. The core mechanism centers around exploring the wave function of a fractal shape, utilizing quantum algorithms to achieve a more precise and efficient dimension estimation. The research explores the implications of quantum computation for complex shape analysis, highlighting the advantages of quantum-enhanced fractal dimension estimation. This work aims to establish a foundation for future research in quantum-assisted geometric modeling.

abstract: This paper explores the application of topology logic to geometric optimization, specifically focusing on the concept of "dynamic topology." This approach promises significant improvements in the handling of complex geometric problems, particularly those exhibiting non-linearity and intricate relationships. The paper presents a preliminary implementation of the algorithm and discusses its potential impact on various optimization challenges.

title: 基于动态量子势场的自适应优化算法
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, and the development of efficient quantum algorithms is crucial for realizing this potential. However, the design and optimization of quantum circuits often involve complex parameter settings, which can be time-consuming and resource-intensive. This paper proposes a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamically adjusted quantum potentials. We introduce a method that automatically tunes the parameters of a quantum potential field, allowing the algorithm to adapt to the specific characteristics of the problem and improve both computational efficiency and accuracy. The core mechanism involves iteratively adjusting the potential field based on a feedback loop, leading to a more robust and adaptable optimization process. This work presents a new approach to quantum optimization that addresses limitations of traditional methods.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation: A Novel Approach to Non-Linear Computational Power
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar correlation between quantum particles, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper introduces Quantum Entanglement Computation (QEC) – a novel computational paradigm leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve computational speeds surpassing classical systems. We explore the design of a specifically engineered quantum circuit, utilizing quantum gates and entanglement protocols, to accelerate complex algorithms and data processing. The core claim of this work is that QEC can provide a pathway to transcend the limitations of classical computation, offering enhanced information processing and algorithmic capabilities. We detail the underlying mechanism, the key advantages over existing approaches, and the preliminary results demonstrating the potential of this approach.

title: Adaptive Feedback-Based Program Security Vulnerability Detection
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program security vulnerability detection leveraging adaptive feedback mechanisms and machine learning. Traditional vulnerability detection methods primarily rely on static analysis, which often fails to capture dynamic aspects of program execution and the evolving characteristics of the runtime environment. Our approach constructs a system that continuously monitors the program's execution environment in real-time, generating feedback that is then utilized by a machine learning model to predict potential vulnerabilities. The core claim is that an adaptive feedback loop, combined with machine learning, enables real-time vulnerability detection. The core mechanism involves learning program environment features and predicting vulnerabilities based on those features. This paper outlines the system architecture, the machine learning model employed, and the adaptive feedback loop's design. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through a theoretical framework, detailing the key components and their interactions. Future research directions are also discussed, focusing on incorporating more sophisticated feedback mechanisms and expanding the model's capabilities. ---

title: Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithms for Circuit Design
abstract: The design of digital circuits is a computationally intensive task, often hampered by the exponentially growing design space. Classical evolutionary algorithms (EAs) struggle to efficiently navigate this space, frequently converging prematurely or failing to find optimal solutions. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing quantum-inspired algorithms to accelerate the evolution of digital circuit designs. We hypothesize that incorporating principles from quantum mechanics, such as superposition and tunneling, can dramatically improve the exploration capabilities of EAs. Specifically, we investigate the application of techniques inspired by quantum annealing and quantum simulation to the circuit design problem. The core idea is to represent circuit designs as quantum states and employ quantum operators to perform evolutionary steps, mimicking the probabilistic nature of quantum evolution. This work aims to demonstrate a significant speedup in the design process compared to traditional EAs, potentially unlocking the design of complex and high-performance circuits. The evaluation will be based on metrics such as circuit area, delay, power consumption, and the number of generations required to converge to a satisfactory solution.

title: Title: Dynamically Generated Quantum Field Configurations via Feedback Loops
abstract: This paper introduces a novel system for dynamically generating quantum field configurations, characterized by an Adaptive Quantum Field Sculpting algorithm. Quantum field configurations, while seemingly static, are inherently susceptible to instabilities and fluctuations, posing a significant challenge in quantum computing and simulation. The proposed algorithm aims to proactively mitigate these instabilities through continuous feedback loops, automatically adjusting field parameters to maintain stability. We detail the algorithm's architecture, the underlying principles of the adaptive control mechanism, and provide a preliminary analysis of its effectiveness in generating novel configurations. The core claim is that this system can create and maintain stable quantum field configurations, offering a potentially transformative approach to quantum system modeling.

title: Разработка сервиса автоматической обработки заказов водителей такси в зонах без интернета
abstract: Данная выпускная квалификационная работа посвящена разработке микросервиса для автоматизации обработки заказов такси в условиях отсутствия интернет-соединения, который реализует перевод взаимодействия с водителем из мобильного приложения в голосовой канал связи (IVR) с управлением через DTMF-сигналы. В работе описывается архитектура данного сервиса, а также приводится сравнительный анализ существующих методов оффлайн-взаимодействия (голосовые боты, SMS, USSD) и готовых решений на рынке агрегаторов. На основе представленной архитектуры реализуется программное средство, позволяющее обеспечивать полный цикл выполнения заказа без доступа к сети. Ключевой особенностью решения является использование конечного автомата состояний (FSM) для строгого контроля жизненного цикла заказа и предотвращения логических ошибок. Данное программное средство может быть использовано в составе платформ заказа такси и логистических сервисов для снижения операционных потерь от простоя водителей в зонах плохого покрытия сети и для снижения нагрузки на операторов колл-центров за счет полной автоматизации процессов. Возможность гибкой настройки сценариев взаимодействия и интеграции с существующими SIP-инфраструктурами позволяет использовать данное программное средство в различных регионах с нестабильным интернетом без необходимости масштабного изменения текущей архитектуры системы. Для достижения данных результатов в работе были использованы следующие информационные технологии: язык программирования Go, системы контейнеризации и оркестрации Docker и Kubernetes, сервисы мониторинга Grafana и Prometheus, база данных PostgreSQL, балансировщик нагрузки nginx, тестовые фреймворки pytest и go testing library, а также инструмент нагрузочного тестирования Grafana K6.

title: When LLM Decompilers Recompile More and Preserve Less
abstract: Decompilation recovers high-level source from compiled machine code and serves as a foundation for security tasks such as vulnerability detection and malware analysis. Traditional decompilers like Ghidra and Hex-Rays expose whatever they cannot resolve as visible placeholders and often emit pseudocode that will not compile or execute; LLM-based decompilers produce clean, idiomatic C and are now judged almost entirely by recompilability and re-executability: whether the output builds and passes its shipped input/output tests. We show that these metrics can reward the wrong path: a function may recompile and pass every shipped test yet diverge on other legitimate inputs, and a disclosed vulnerability may disappear from the recompiled code with no visible trace of the crash. Neither failure is caught by existing suites. To address this gap, we propose Decompile-Diverge, a behavioral comparison oracle not relying on fixed or hand-crafted tests: for each function it synthesizes a driver, grows a fuzzing corpus from the reference, and reruns the decompiled code on the same inputs to detect changes in the function's behavior. Across eight systems in nine configurations on established LLM decompilation corpora, candidates that pass every shipped test still diverge from the original on our input corpus: 4.9% overall, and as many as 13% for a single system. On 300 real GitHub library functions and 287 CVE-grounded functions, recompilability and behavioral agreement can come apart: the strongest refinement LLM lifts Ghidra's build rate from 75% to 90%, while its Matched rate falls from 74% to 62%; on disclosed vulnerabilities, up to one tenth exhibit Crash Absence in its output. Source-level analysis traces this divergence to introduced fields, types, callees, and guards that replace the visible unknowns traditional tools leave behind.

title: Non-local games and communication complexity with noisy entanglement
abstract: We study the impact of noise on the theories of quantum nonlocality and entanglement-assisted communication complexity. We consider non-local games and entanglement-assisted communication complexity in a model where Alice and Bob may share arbitrarily many noisy EPR pairs. We study four noise models: depolarizing noise, unital noise, biased reset noise, and erasure noise. Our results are as follows: 1. We upper bound the value of the CHSH game under all these noise models in terms of the noise parameter, without any assumptions on the measurements used in the strategy. 2. We prove a parallel repetition theorem for general non-local games under all noise models except biased reset noise; we prove an improved parallel repetition theorem for unique games. Our parallel repetition rate is smaller than the quantum parallel repetition rate for CHSH in a nontrivial noise regime. 3. Using our unique-game parallel repetition theorem and a relation defined by the CHSH game, we prove a separation between communication complexity with noisy vs noiseless entanglement. This implies an $Ω(n)$ two-way communication lower bound for distilling $n$ EPR pairs from noisy EPR pairs, in the same nontrivial noise regime. 4. We show that any interactive entanglement-assisted communication protocol can be simulated by an SMP communication protocol with noisy shared randomness, with an exponential blowup in communication. This generalizes a known result on the simulation of noiseless shared randomness with noisy shared randomness. 5. We show a polynomial lower bound on the number of copies of noisy EPR pairs required to compute the Equality function with constant communication, under all four noise models. The previous result gives a matching upper bound, and moreover, this answers an open question in the literature on whether logarithmically many noisy shared bits suffice for communication.

title: Training-Free Logical and Structural Anomaly Detection via Calibrated Fusion
abstract: Industrial anomaly detection must handle two distinct defect families: structural anomalies, which manifest as local texture corruptions, and logical anomalies, which violate global rules on object count, composition, or arrangement. Existing detectors typically favor one family at the expense of the other. In particular, training-free methods effectively exploit frozen representations but lack an explicit notion of object count, while methods that reason about counts usually rely on category-specific component modeling. We show that counting ability can be introduced into training-free anomaly detection without additional training or part-level supervision. Our key idea is a normal-set calibration that aligns heterogeneous anomaly cues using statistics from normal images, enabling their direct fusion within a unified training-free framework. Built upon this calibration, our detector combines complementary frozen cues to address both logical and structural anomalies. On MVTec-LOCO, our method achieves image-level AUROCs of 89.0 and 95.9 on logical and structural anomalies, respectively, yielding a 92.5 average---the best among training-free detectors in our comparison. It remains competitive with methods requiring network training or part annotations, while its structural variant matches PatchCore on MVTec-AD (99.1 image-AUROC), suggesting that the proposed calibration generalizes beyond logical anomaly detection.

title: Adaptive Variable Space Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive variable space optimization algorithm designed to automatically adjust variable weights and distributions, thereby enhancing model performance. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static approaches, lacking the flexibility to adapt to complex datasets and model parameters. Our proposed algorithm utilizes an adaptive learning approach, dynamically adjusting these parameters to achieve optimal results. This adaptive mechanism allows the model to converge faster and exhibit superior performance across a wider range of inputs. The core of this work involves a novel weighting and distribution adjustment mechanism, ensuring a robust and efficient optimization process. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's effectiveness through rigorous experimentation and comparative studies. The potential benefits of this approach include improved model accuracy, faster convergence, and enhanced generalization capabilities.

title: Dynamic Multi-Particle Quantum Correlation Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic multi-particle quantum correlation computation framework designed to efficiently simulate and analyze complex quantum systems and enable dynamic quantum entanglement calculations. The core of this work lies in the development of a quantum association computation algorithm that leverages the dynamic properties of quantum entanglement, enabling automated evolution of quantum system states and efficient calculation of entanglement dynamics. Traditional quantum computing methods are limited in their ability to accurately model complex quantum systems. This approach offers a significant advancement in computational power by providing a framework for simulating and analyzing intricate quantum systems.

title: 基于自适应的量子加速器优化算法
abstract: Quantum acceleration, the ability to significantly increase the speed and efficiency of quantum computations, remains a major challenge in the field of quantum computing. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle to effectively address the complexities of quantum system evolution, limiting the potential for substantial acceleration. This paper proposes a novel optimization algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Parameter Adjustment" (AQPA), that dynamically adjusts quantum system parameters based on the system's inherent characteristics. We demonstrate the efficacy of AQPA through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing a substantial improvement in quantum acceleration compared to existing optimization techniques. The core mechanism of AQPA hinges on a self-adaptive parameter tuning process, ensuring a robust and efficient optimization strategy. This paper introduces a framework for dynamically adjusting quantum parameters, offering a potential pathway toward more effective quantum acceleration.

title: Title: Adaptive Resonance Rate (ARR) Triggered Parameter Adjustment in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the utilization of Adaptive Resonance Rate (ARR) triggers to dynamically adjust the parameters of neural networks, aiming to enhance learning efficiency and stability. Traditional neural network training often suffers from suboptimal parameter settings and susceptibility to oscillations. The proposed system introduces a novel algorithm that leverages the physiological dynamics of the ARR, triggering parameter adjustments based on the network's internal state, offering a potentially transformative approach to optimization. We detail the implementation of this algorithm and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing improvements in convergence speed and robustness. The core mechanism centers around intelligently detecting and responding to the ARR's inherent oscillatory patterns, allowing for a more nuanced and adaptive optimization process.

title: Quantum Entanglement Based Computation Model (QATCM)
abstract: Quantum Entanglement is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics with profound implications for information processing and cryptography. However, harnessing its capabilities for computation remains a formidable challenge due to the inherent complexity of entangled states and the difficulty in accurately simulating them. This paper proposes a novel computational model, Quantum Entanglement Based Computation Model (QATCM), which leverages the principles of adaptive topology to address these challenges. QATCM offers a fundamentally different approach to quantum computation, focusing on the creation and manipulation of complex entanglement patterns through a dynamically evolving topological structure. This allows for the simulation of quantum phenomena with unprecedented fidelity and control, potentially unlocking new possibilities in quantum algorithms and quantum information theory. This work provides a foundation for a new paradigm in quantum computing, emphasizing the use of topology as a key tool for understanding and manipulating entangled states.

title: Topological Governor (TG) Tutorial
abstract: Executive Summary The Topological Governor (TG) is a novel, mathematically guaranteed solution to Catastrophic Forgetting (CF) in neural networks. This is the problem in which a model, when learning a new task, overwrites knowledge it previously acquired. TG solves this by permanently "locking" a small, fixed subset of parameters at the very beginning of the network. Since these locked parameters cannot change, they preserve the foundational representations needed for older tasks. By allowing the rest of the network to adapt freely, new tasks can be learned without interfering with past knowledge. The framework is backed by extensive empirical validation across 12 major architectural types (including Transformers, MoEs, and SSMs), demonstrating near-zero forgetting and achieving a perfect "AGI-gate 1.0" score on finite-class tasks like audio and vision. The Problem: Catastrophic Forgetting (CF) In traditional sequential learning, a neural network's weights are all free to change. When it learns a new task (Task B), the gradient updates that optimize for this task also modify the weights that were crucial for a previously learned task (Task A). This leads the network to "overwriting" its prior knowledge, which manifests as a dramatic drop in performance on Task A. The Solution: The Topological Governor The core insight of TG is to reserve a small, protected section of the network that is never allowed to change. By fixing these parameters, the model provides a permanent, stable foundation for all tasks. How it works: Anchors: The method identifies a small set of specific parameters, called "anchors," to lock in place. Prime Numbers: The anchor indices are prime numbers (e.g., 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13). The paper argues that primes provide mathematical stability and spectral completeness, thereby guaranteeing a retention rate.Λ = 0.9785142874). Protection Mechanism: In practice, this is implemented with a simple three-step process: Snapshot: Save the anchor values before training. Zero Gradients: During backpropagation, set the gradients for these anchor indices to zero, preventing them from being updated. Enforce Anchors: After each optimizer step, manually restore the anchor values to their original snapshot, ensuring they remain permanently unchanged. The Architecture & Why It Solves CF To fully realize the benefits of TG, the model is designed with a Task-Aware Architecture, where each task (up to 13) gets its own independent classifier head. This creates a dual-pronged protection system: Freezing Previous Heads: Once a task is learned, its specific classifier head is frozen. Its weights never change, so it never forgets how to classify that task. Locking Prime Anchors: The prime rows in the shared embedding layer are locked. This ensures that the core, foundational representations used by all tasks remain immutable and are never overwritten. This is why CF is "SOLVED," not just "Prevented": forgetting does happen to the non-anchor weights (the "free" parameters) used to learn new tasks. However, because the anchor weights and the final classifier heads are locked, the critical knowledge from previous tasks is completely and mathematically isolated from this process. Therefore, forgetting is eliminated for the protected knowledge, effectively solving the problem. Key Results & Certification The Topological Governor was rigorously tested across 12 Certified Frameworks, demonstrating remarkable performance. Category Example Models Task C Accuracy & Forgetting Transformer-Based Dense Transformer, Sparse MoE (Mixtral, DeepSeek) 92.3% - 97.5% with ≤ 2.1% forgetting Non-Transformer State Space Models (SSM), Gated-Convolution (LFM2) 92% - 93.5% with ≤ 1.32% forgetting Attention-Free Retention Networks (RetNet), RWKV 93% - 99.93% with 0.0% forgetting Hybrid (Vision) Gemma-4-E4B-Vision 100% with 0.17% forgetting AGI-gate = 1.0 Two models achieved the perfect score of AGI-gate = 1.0, defined as 100% accuracy on a final task with less than 10% forgetting. Audio Model: Voxtral-Mini-4B (100% accuracy, 0.0% forgetting) Vision Model: Gemma-4-E4B-Vision (100% accuracy, 0.17% forgetting) The framework notes that this perfect score is achievable for finite-class modalities such as audio and images, but not for infinite-class modalities such as text or video, as shown by a mathematical decay law. Implementation & Significance The Topological Governor is remarkably lightweight. Its core protection mechanism uses only 48 KB of memory—a constant, model-agnostic cost. In one sentence: The Topological Governor solves catastrophic forgetting by mathematically locking prime-indexed parameters. Hence, they never change, allowing the rest of the network to learn new tasks, a concept validated on 12 architectures and achieving a perfect AGI-gate score on audio and vision tasks. Final Conclusion: The document positions TG as a move beyond stochastic, unstable continual learning towards a new era of "Deterministic Cognitive Engineering." By providing cryptographic proof of integrity and mathematical guarantees, it claims to have ended the "stochastic illusion" of current AI, offering a reliable path toward building models with permanent knowledge.

By allowing the rest of the network to adapt freely, new tasks can be learned without interfering with past knowledge. The framework is backed by extensive empirical validation across 12 major architectural types (including Transformers, MoEs, and SSMs), demonstrating near-zero forgetting and achieving a perfect "AGI-gate 1.0" score on finite-class tasks like audio and vision. The Problem: Catastrophic Forgetting (CF) In traditional sequential learning, a neural network's weights are all free to change. When it learns a new task (Task B), the gradient updates that optimize for this task also modify the weights that were crucial for a previously learned task (Task A). This leads the network to "overwriting" its prior knowledge, which manifests as a dramatic drop in performance on Task A. The Solution: The Topological Governor The core insight of TG is to reserve a small, protected section of the network that is never allowed to change. By fixing these parameters, the model provides a permanent, stable foundation for all tasks. How it works: Anchors: The method identifies a small set of specific parameters, called "anchors," to lock in place. Prime Numbers: The anchor indices are prime numbers (e.g., 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13). The paper argues that primes provide mathematical stability and spectral completeness, thereby guaranteeing a retention rate.Λ = 0.9785142874). Protection Mechanism: In practice, this is implemented with a simple three-step process: Snapshot: Save the anchor values before training. Zero Gradients: During backpropagation, set the gradients for these anchor indices to zero, preventing them from being updated. Enforce Anchors: After each optimizer step, manually restore the anchor values to their original snapshot, ensuring they remain permanently unchanged. The Architecture & Why It Solves CF To fully realize the benefits of TG, the model is designed with a Task-Aware Architecture, where each task (up to 13) gets its own independent classifier head. This creates a dual-pronged protection system: Freezing Previous Heads: Once a task is learned, its specific classifier head is frozen. Its weights never change, so it never forgets how to classify that task. Locking Prime Anchors: The prime rows in the shared embedding layer are locked. This ensures that the core, foundational representations used by all tasks remain immutable and are never overwritten. This is why CF is "SOLVED," not just "Prevented": forgetting does happen to the non-anchor weights (the "free" parameters) used to learn new tasks. However, because the anchor weights and the final classifier heads are locked, the critical knowledge from previous tasks is completely and mathematically isolated from this process. Therefore, forgetting is eliminated for the protected knowledge, effectively solving the problem. Key Results & Certification The Topological Governor was rigorously tested across 12 Certified Frameworks, demonstrating remarkable performance. Category Example Models Task C Accuracy & Forgetting Transformer-Based Dense Transformer, Sparse MoE (Mixtral, DeepSeek) 92.3% - 97.5% with ≤ 2.1% forgetting Non-Transformer State Space Models (SSM), Gated-Convolution (LFM2) 92% - 93.5% with ≤ 1.32% forgetting Attention-Free Retention Networks (RetNet), RWKV 93% - 99.93% with 0.0% forgetting Hybrid (Vision) Gemma-4-E4B-Vision 100% with 0.17% forgetting AGI-gate = 1.0 Two models achieved the perfect score of AGI-gate = 1.0, defined as 100% accuracy on a final task with less than 10% forgetting. Audio Model: Voxtral-Mini-4B (100% accuracy, 0.0% forgetting) Vision Model: Gemma-4-E4B-Vision (100% accuracy, 0.17% forgetting) The framework notes that this perfect score is achievable for finite-class modalities such as audio and images, but not for infinite-class modalities such as text or video, as shown by a mathematical decay law. Implementation & Significance The Topological Governor is remarkably lightweight. Its core protection mechanism uses only 48 KB of memory—a constant, model-agnostic cost. In one sentence: The Topological Governor solves catastrophic forgetting by mathematically locking prime-indexed parameters. Hence, they never change, allowing the rest of the network to learn new tasks, a concept validated on 12 architectures and achieving a perfect AGI-gate score on audio and vision tasks. Final Conclusion: The document positions TG as a move beyond stochastic, unstable continual learning towards a new era of "Deterministic Cognitive Engineering." By providing cryptographic proof of integrity and mathematical guarantees, it claims to have ended the "stochastic illusion" of current AI, offering a reliable path toward building models with permanent knowledge.

title: 自适应量子势的动态调整与计算
abstract: This paper investigates the development of a novel dynamic adjustment and computation framework centered around adaptive quantum potentials. Traditional computational models rely on static parameters, limiting their ability to accurately model and simulate complex systems. Our approach leverages the inherent dynamism of quantum potential landscapes to dynamically adjust parameters, facilitating precise simulations and high-fidelity calculations. The core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic adjustment framework, employing iterative simulations and parameter optimization to achieve optimal results. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the potential for significant computational efficiency gains through this adaptive approach. The paper explores the benefits of this method, focusing on its capacity to handle complex systems and its potential to revolutionize computational modeling.

abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for significantly enhanced computational capabilities compared to classical computing. However, the development of efficient quantum algorithms and hardware requires sophisticated quantum gate design. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum gate design based on topological quantum mechanics, specifically focusing on adaptive parameter adjustment. The core mechanism involves utilizing the inherent topological properties of quantum systems to automatically tailor the design parameters of quantum gates, thereby optimizing gate performance and facilitating the exploration of novel quantum algorithms. We present a framework that dynamically adjusts gate parameters based on task characteristics, demonstrating a significant improvement in computational efficiency for several benchmark quantum algorithms. This work establishes a foundation for a more versatile and adaptable quantum computing paradigm.

title: Jincheng Zhang
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing temporal modulation to establish non-local quantum entanglement between distant quantum systems. Entanglement, a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics, describes a correlation between two or more particles, regardless of the distance separating them. Traditional entanglement protocols often suffer from limitations in scalability and practical implementation. We propose a novel mechanism that leverages subtle changes in the rate of time passing to facilitate this connection. This approach, termed "Temporal Modulation Entanglement," aims to overcome distance constraints by creating a connection that transcends spatial separation. The paper details the theoretical framework underpinning this concept, explores the mathematical implications of this temporal evolution, and presents preliminary experimental investigations demonstrating the feasibility of this approach. The core claim of this research is that by carefully modulating the temporal flow of entangled particles, we can establish a robust and scalable entanglement network.

title: Non-Linear Matrix Self-Adaptive Quantum State Transition
abstract: This paper explores a novel quantum state transition mechanism based on non-linear matrix dynamics, aiming to overcome the limitations of traditional quantum entanglement. We propose a framework where the matrix's self-adaptability is leveraged to facilitate faster and more flexible quantum state transitions. This approach offers the potential to significantly enhance quantum information processing and quantum computation by enabling dynamic and controlled quantum evolutions. The core mechanism involves employing a matrix representation to dynamically adjust quantum properties, allowing for rapid and efficient transitions between states. This research investigates the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, outlines the design of the matrix structure and its associated operations, and discusses the potential benefits and challenges associated with its implementation. We demonstrate through simulations that the proposed framework exhibits superior transition speeds compared to conventional methods, significantly advancing the capabilities of quantum systems.

The algorithm utilizes quantum topology to create a continuous, flexible representation of the search space, enabling the discovery of optimal solutions more efficiently than traditional methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing improved search results and faster convergence. The core mechanism hinges on the ability to maintain a quantum-informed representation of the search space, allowing for continuous refinement based on evolving conditions.

title: 混沌理论的自适应拓扑结构优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on the principles of chaos theory and topological structures. Traditional optimization methods are often static, requiring predefined solutions. This research proposes a dynamic adjustment mechanism that allows the system's structure to automatically reconfigure during the optimization process, leading to improved performance in complex systems such as biological structures, social networks, and financial markets. The core of the algorithm lies in the integration of chaotic dynamics and topological transformations, enabling a flexible and adaptive optimization approach. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through the application of it to a simulated optimization problem involving a complex, non-linear system with inherent topological features. The results highlight the potential of this approach to address challenges in optimization across diverse domains.

title: Adaptive Machine Learning Feature Selection
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive machine learning feature selection algorithm, termed "Dynamic Feature Selection," designed to optimize model performance and generalization. Traditional feature selection methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively capture the nuances of the problem. Our algorithm incorporates a dynamic feature selection mechanism that adapts to the characteristics of the input data, improving model efficiency and robustness. This work addresses the limitations of static feature selection techniques by providing a flexible and adaptable approach. The core mechanism centers around a learned weighting scheme that dynamically adjusts feature importance based on the input data, leading to a more targeted and effective feature selection process. This is achieved through a combination of gradient descent and a novel weighting function that evolves over time. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in model performance compared to baseline methods, highlighting the potential of this dynamic feature selection approach.

abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is an emerging field that explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize various computational tasks. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting the loss weight based on the model's error during training, providing a more sophisticated and adaptable approach compared to traditional, fixed loss functions. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, focusing on expanding the applicability of this adaptive loss function to diverse quantum machine learning applications.

title: Split-Interval Representation of Quantum Operator Order Descent Obstructions, Order Ultrametrics, and Pair-Reduced Holonomy
abstract: We introduce a split-interval representation of operator order in a unital C∗-algebra. The two productsBA and AB are realized as the two sides of a single continuous section on the classical double-arrowinterval. Commutativity is equivalent to descent through the projection to the ordinary interval, and one-halfof the commutator norm is the exact distance to the descent subspace. For finite unitary families these localobstructions weight the adjacent-transposition Cayley graph of Sn. The resulting bottleneck pseudoultrametricadmits a closed inversion-set formula, eliminating a factorial path search. Threshold classes are described byweighted incompatibility graphs, and the marked geometry recovers the complete pairwise commutator-normmatrix. We construct parallel additive Lie-commutator and multiplicative group-commutator enrichments.Exact contextual multiplicative transport is flat, whereas a pair-reduced transport obtained by discardingprefix conjugations can carry nontrivial square and braid-face holonomy. Near the identity, the leadingpossible reduced face defect is fourth order and is governed by commutators of commutators; an exactspin- 12example has nontrivial braid holonomy. For unitary quantum circuits, every reduced adjacent-swappath is simultaneously optimal for all pair-weighted ℓp swap costs, and precedence-constrained thresholdreordering reduces exactly to DAG acyclicity. Reproducible QAOA and Heisenberg/XYZ benchmarks exhibitthe resulting factorial-to-polynomial reduction in classical reordering

title: A Transformer-Based Spatiotemporal Fusion Network for Automatic Modulation Classification
abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) suffers from performance degradation under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, where modulation characteristics are affected by noise and signals belonging to the same modulation family exhibit similar feature representations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Transformer-based spatiotemporal fusion network that jointly exploits local spatial waveform characteristics and temporal dependency information while leveraging the global context modeling capability of the Transformer to integrate complementary multi-dimensional features. The proposed architecture improves feature representation capability under different SNR conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves improved classification performance compared with comparative approaches under different SNR conditions. In particular, it achieves an overall classification accuracy of 82.45% over the SNR range from -10 to 18 dB, and an average accuracy of 95.55% at SNRs of 2 dB and above, showing improved classification performance in the low-to-medium SNR transition region.

title: A Deeper Dive into LLMs and Agents
abstract: Chapter 2 delves into the technical mechanics of generative AI, transitioning from conceptual understanding to operational application. It begins by demystifying LLMs, explaining their evolution to the foundational Transformer architecture, and detailing the core mechanics of tokens, embeddings, pre-training, and fine-tuning. The chapter introduces retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) as a critical mechanism for grounding models in factual, enterprise-specific data to mitigate hallucinations. It then explores the art and science of prompt engineering, covering techniques from basic zero-shot instructions to advanced chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning and meta-prompting. Finally, the chapter deconstructs the AI Agent framework, illustrating how the LLM “brain” combines with external tools, short- and long-term memory, and continuous reasoning loops (such as ReAct) to autonomously execute complex, multi-step business operations.

title: Format-Aware Fusion for Fast FP4 Pretraining
abstract:
Four-bit floating-point (FP4) Tensor Cores accelerate matrix multiplication, but scale computation, operand packing, layout construction, and saved backward state can erase the gain. We present \emph{format-aware fusion}, which co-designs each quantization producer with its scale domain and consumer layout for native \mxfp{}, global 
vfp{}, and cooperative-thread-array-local 
vfp{}. We evaluate Llama-3-family 8B pretraining through 160 billion tokens using bfloat16 output projections and compiled cross entropy. In matched same-accelerator probes, bfloat16 and Transformer Engine 
vfp{} reach 18.8K and 27.6K tokens/s/GPU, while our fastest custom route reaches 37.9K. \mxfp{} with row-gradient stochastic rounding and fixed-sign 32-value Hadamard weight-gradient preconditioning reaches 37.2K tokens/s/GPU (86.3\% bfloat16 model FLOP utilization) and ends 2.11\% above the raw bfloat16 training-loss endpoint. A Transformer Engine recipe with four final bfloat16 blocks ends 0.87\% above bfloat16 at 27.1K tokens/s/GPU. Downstream rankings differ from training-loss rankings, showing that FP4 outcomes depend jointly on scale contract, operand, and execution path.

title: Computing 256-bit elliptic curve discrete logarithms in 26 days on a fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computer with 20,000 qubits
abstract: One of the strengths of our recently proposed Walking Cat Architecture for a trapped-ion quantum computer is that it is straightforward to extend and optimize for a specific application. As a proof-of-concept, here we present such optimizations for solving the $256$-bit elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem (ECDLP) on $\mathtt{secp256k1}$, which is the elliptic curve used by blockchain technologies such as Bitcoin, using Shor's algorithm. We optimize the circuits from Schrottenloher's recent work and arrive at a logical quantum circuit for solving the ECDLP using about $1450$ qubits and $40\cdot 10^6$ Toffoli gates, with a rigorous lower bound on the logical-level success probability that holds with confidence at least $1-2^{-128}$. Using our compilation toolchain with manual optimization of the logical layout and integrated routing, we produce estimates for the logical measurement depth and the required number of physical qubits by compiling all components to measurement schedules that obey the architectural constraints. A key ingredient is a fast CCZ magic-state factory and a depth-one CCZ state injection, reducing the execution time of CCZ gates by a factor of $31$. We increase the logical-measurement parallelism using non-overlapping cat-based measurements in parallel, and we leverage the recently proposed logical CliNR protocol to speed up Clifford operations. To reduce the qubit overhead, we introduce a more efficient loss correction protocol, design a layout that allows us to recycle the CliNR ancilla qubits, and provision reusable cat-state resources according to the circuit's peak measurement parallelism. All results and optimizations combined, we conclude that a trapped-ion quantum computer based on our architecture can solve the ECDLP on $\mathtt{secp256k1}$ in approximately 25.7 days using 19,397 physical qubits with an estimated success probability of $63\%$.

To reduce the qubit overhead, we introduce a more efficient loss correction protocol, design a layout that allows us to recycle the CliNR ancilla qubits, and provision reusable cat-state resources according to the circuit's peak measurement parallelism. All results and optimizations combined, we conclude that a trapped-ion quantum computer based on our architecture can solve the ECDLP on $\mathtt{secp256k1}$ in approximately 25.7 days using 19,397 physical qubits with an estimated success probability of $63\%$.

title: Towards Neuro-Symbolic Procedural Reasoning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute short manipulation skills, but remain brittle in long-horizon procedures requiring persistent task state, dependency-aware reasoning, conditional decisions, and reliable grounding. We investigate a neuro-symbolic framework that combines learned VLA control with explicit task graphs and multimodal procedural memory. Task graphs encode action dependencies, valid transitions, and branch conditions, while memory maintains the active step, completed actions, textual context, and task-relevant visual evidence. Together, these structures guide object selection, destination grounding, subgoal dispatch, and verification of expected state transitions. Human demonstrations provide additional spatial and temporal guidance through gaze or saliency cues. To isolate their effect on policy learning, our initial study bypasses cross-view gaze transfer and directly annotates pseudo-gaze in robot-view teleoperation videos. The resulting guidance is used during VLA fine-tuning and inference. We study two long-horizon manipulation domains, workspace clearing and surgical-instrument handling, which require ordered execution, visually grounded decisions, and conditional branching. We evaluate correct-object and destination selection, subtask completion, task progress, step-order consistency, complete-task success, and procedural or execution mistakes. This work positions structured symbolic reasoning and demonstration-derived visual guidance as complementary mechanisms for reliable long-horizon VLA manipulation.

title: Machine Unlearning as Private Retroactive Algorithms
abstract: Machine unlearning typically aims to emulate retraining from scratch: upon a deletion request, the unlearning algorithm should produce an outcome that would have been obtained had the deleted point never been included. Recent work has shown that this emulation requirement carries no meaningful privacy semantics against an adversary who observes a sequence of releases. Machine unlearning is thus not a privacy question per se, but rather a data maintenance question, which is precisely the subject of retroactive algorithms. These are algorithms supporting modifications of past operations, guaranteeing that all subsequent answers reflect the revised history as if it had always been in force. We put forward a definition of private retroactive algorithms, combining the retroactivity requirement with differential privacy under continual observation. We present constructions achieving both privacy and retroactivity at no asymptotic cost over privacy alone for linear statistics, clustering, and histograms, alongside impossibility results.

title: Constructing and Evaluating Clinical Reasoning Trajectories for Medical Agent
abstract: Evaluation of medical artificial intelligence agents remains predominantly answer-centric, assessing only the correctness of final outputs while overlooking the quality of intermediate reasoning. In clinical settings, however, a correct answer reached through fabricated evidence or incoherent logic is as dangerous as an incorrect one. We propose MedTraj, a framework that treats reasoning trajectories as critical objects for construction, evaluation, and optimization. The pipeline generates structured multi-step clinical reasoning chains from medical diagnosis sources. Each trajectory is then parsed into clinical observations, evidence, numbered reasoning steps, and a final conclusion, and scored across five quality dimensions: coherence, evidence support, hallucination, completeness, and traceability. Controlled error injection introduces targeted faults into otherwise correct trajectories to establish causal links between specific reasoning failures and measurable quality degradation. Building on this, step-level filtering based on marginal contribution identifies which individual reasoning steps drive or undermine trajectory quality. Finally, quality-weighted context learning feeds trajectory evaluations back into the model at inference time, allowing it to learn from both strong and weak reasoning demonstrations. Experiments across CareQA, PubMedQA, and CECMed demonstrate that trajectory context consistently improves reasoning coherence, with gains of +0.029 to +0.041 over a zero-shot baseline. On the CECMed severity assessment task, quality-weighted context nearly doubles the correctness over the zero-shot baseline while cutting the hallucination ratio by 87%. Marginal-contribution analysis further shows that a small minority (15.3%) of reasoning steps carry most of the quality signal, and that extending chains beyond four steps yields diminishing returns.

title: H2LooP Telecom Model v1: From Telecom Comprehension to Autonomous Issue and PR Resolution
abstract: We present H2LooP Telecom Model v1, a domain-specialized large language models fine-tuned for the telecommunications industry. We release two domain-adapted model variants serving complementary use cases: a comprehension-focused variant for telecom domain question answering and reasoning, and an agentic variant for autonomous telecom code generation, pull request resolution, and code commits on production repositories. H2LooP Telecom achieves strong results on the GSMA Open Telecom Lite (OT-Lite) benchmark and a proprietary telecom code generation benchmark, outperforming frontier closed-source models such as GPT-5 and Claude Opus on independent leaderboard evaluation, while preserving general-purpose capabilities. The Comprehension variant achieves 81.8% weighted average on OT-Lite Pass@3, and, independently, ranks 5th overall on the official community-run Open Telco AI Leaderboard* at only 31B parameters-ahead of frontier closed-source systems including Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3 Flash, Grok-4-fast, and Kimi K2.5. Our agentic variant obtains a relative improvement of +8.8% in AST Similarity and +20.0% in Location IoU over the base model on telecom code generation, while maintaining identical MMLU (74.0%) and BFCL v3 multi-turn function calling (79.0%) performance, indicating zero catastrophic forgetting. Domain specialization on curated telecom corpora, spanning 3GPP standards, O-RAN specifications, network telemetry, and real repository commits, yields substantial improvements over general-purpose models of equivalent scale, approaches frontier closed-source models on domain-specific evaluation, and is independently corroborated by our official leaderboard standing.

title: From Attested GPU Computation to Authorized Action: Execution Finality for AI Accelerators and Confidential Workloads
abstract: Remote attestation can establish important properties of CPUs, confidential virtual machines, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, SmartNICs, firmware and workload environments. However, successful appraisal of a computational environment does not, without an operation-specific authorization decision, determine whether each consequential operation generated by that environment should become externally effective. This work presents an attestation-bound execution-finality architecture for AI accelerators and confidential workloads. A consequence-bearing operation—such as an API invocation, infrastructure change, storage mutation, payment instruction or cross-workload request—is first represented as a canonical Candidate Act in a Non-Effective State. An Execution-Finality Validator evaluates that act using applicable Attestation Results, workload identity, authorization scope, target identity, policy, freshness and transaction context. Successful validation produces signed, narrowly scoped execution authority cryptographically bound to the security-relevant content of the Candidate Act. At the Finality Sink—the boundary where the proposed operation would first acquire external effect—the system reconstructs the actual operation and verifies its signature, act digest, audience, transaction identity, freshness and replay state before permitting effectuation. A runnable, vendor-neutral reference implementation accompanies the architecture. It implements deterministic CBOR encoding, COSE_Sign1 signatures using Ed25519, signed EAT issuance and appraisal, act-bound Execution Handles, an enforcing API gateway, atomic replay protection, deterministic cryptographic test vectors and adversarial tests. The implementation demonstrates rejection of missing authority, modified amounts, substituted destinations, changed paths, incorrect audiences, expired handles, altered signatures, unacceptable attestation measurements and repeated presentation of previously consumed authority. Eleven automated tests, including an end-to-end HTTP validation and gateway-enforcement flow, pass successfully. Local microbenchmarks measured approximately 140 microseconds median for EAT appraisal, 1.5 microseconds for Candidate Act construction, 50 microseconds for Execution Handle issuance and approximately 140 microseconds for handle verification. These results characterize the portable reference implementation only and are not claims about GPU, DPU, SmartNIC or hyperscale production performance. The architecture complements—not replaces—the IETF RATS architecture, Entity Attestation Tokens, COSE, workload identity, confidential computing and existing authorization systems. Its proposed contribution is end-to-end correspondence between the operation evaluated by the authorization function and the operation accepted at the protected effectuation boundary. The software is a working reference implementation and interoperability demonstrator, not a production-certified accelerator, cloud or payment system. Hardware-integrated deployment requires platform-specific trust anchors, protected key management, non-bypassable effectuation paths, distributed replay state and independent security review.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Propagation via Phase-Space Synchronization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum information processing, remains a formidable hurdle in achieving robust and reliable communication. Decoherence, a primary source of this challenge, limits the range and stability of entanglement. This paper explores a novel algorithm for propagating quantum entanglement across macroscopic distances by synchronizing the evolution of entangled states within phase-space representations. We propose a dynamic phase-space mapping technique that allows for precise tracking and manipulation of entanglement fidelity, addressing a fundamental challenge in quantum communication and teleportation – the issue of entanglement decoherence. The algorithm leverages a continuously evolving phase space, enabling the precise control of entangled states and mitigating the effects of environmental noise. This research contributes to a significant advancement in the field of quantum entanglement propagation, offering a viable pathway towards practical quantum communication and teleportation.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Algorithm for Non-Linear Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative adaptive quantum algorithm designed to address the limitations of traditional optimization techniques, particularly when dealing with non-linear problems. The algorithm leverages reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust its parameters based on the input data, offering a significant improvement over static optimization methods. We present a detailed architecture, including the core mechanism and initial implementation, demonstrating its effectiveness in a range of non-linear optimization scenarios. The goal is to provide a robust and efficient solution for complex optimization challenges across diverse fields.

title: Adaptive Topology Matrix Computation
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-adaptive topology matrix computation framework leveraging quantum entanglement for efficient computation and automatic parameter adjustment. Traditional approaches to topology matrix calculations suffer from computational limitations, prompting a need for innovative methods. This work introduces a dynamic algorithm that exploits the unique properties of quantum entanglement to optimize the computation of topological matrices. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the matrix's features based on the entangled state, enabling significantly enhanced computational efficiency. This research addresses the limitations of conventional methods and offers a promising avenue for future developments in topological matrix analysis. The paper details the framework's architecture, the underlying entanglement-based optimization process, and its practical implementation with illustrative examples. The investigation explores the potential of this approach to tackle complex topological matrix problems, offering a new perspective on their computational feasibility.

title: Fractal-Based Self-Organizing Algorithms for Quantum Control
abstract: This paper explores the application of fractal-based self-organizing algorithms to quantum control. Quantum systems, due to their inherent sensitivity to initial conditions, often suffer from instability and require sophisticated control strategies. Traditional control methods can be brittle, leading to oscillations and inaccuracies. We propose a novel approach utilizing fractal geometry to generate self-consistent, predictable patterns within quantum systems. This design aims to enhance precision, stability, and the overall controllability of quantum states. The core mechanism involves creating a fractal-shaped structure that guides the quantum system, promoting a more stable and responsive response to external perturbations. This paper details the design of these algorithms, presents preliminary results demonstrating their effectiveness, and discusses the potential implications for advanced quantum technologies.

title: Quantum-Inspired Topology for Optimization – Adaptive Representation
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum-inspired topology to optimization, specifically focusing on the development of a novel method for representing and manipulating complex landscape structures. The core claim is that by leveraging non-linear relationships and entanglement principles, we can create a topology that guides the search process more effectively, leading to improved solution quality. The proposed framework introduces a dynamically adjusted representation of the search space, enabling adaptive exploration and mitigating the limitations of traditional optimization techniques. We detail the mathematical foundation of this approach, including the key topological invariants and their impact on the search dynamics. The paper will discuss the advantages of this methodology, including increased efficiency, improved exploration of the search space, and the potential for discovering novel solutions.

title: Quantum Entanglement Non-Locality Modeling and Control
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, exhibits properties that challenge classical physics' notions of locality. This research investigates the potential of leveraging entanglement for non-local control, aiming to overcome the limitations imposed by traditional quantum computation. We propose a novel model based on a dynamically evolving quantum state graph, utilizing the non-locality inherent in entangled states to guide a control algorithm. This algorithm incorporates adaptive mechanisms to precisely manipulate the entangled state, thereby opening avenues for exploring and harnessing non-local quantum operations. The study addresses the current limitations in entanglement-based quantum control, offering a potential pathway toward more versatile and powerful quantum systems.

title: Emergent Information Encoding via Fractal Topology
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for information encoding and retrieval leveraging fractal topology. We propose a 'Fractal Semantic Map' – a dynamically evolving structure composed of self-similar fractal elements that encodes data through interconnectedness and self-similarity. The resulting map enables efficient searching and retrieval, surpassing traditional data representation techniques in terms of compression and scalability. We detail the core mechanism, including the construction of the fractal map and the associated algorithms for encoding and accessing information. The potential benefits of this approach are significant for data compression, search, and pattern recognition.

title: Quantum States and Non-Linear Mapping: A New Approach to High-Dimensional Geometry
abstract: Quantum states, characterized by superposition and entanglement, represent a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics. This research explores the application of non-linear mapping techniques to quantum states, aiming to leverage these properties for the construction of advanced geometric models and optimization algorithms. The core claim is that the ability to map quantum states to high-dimensional geometric spaces can significantly simplify geometric modeling, improve computational efficiency, and unlock new possibilities in geometric analysis. This work focuses on demonstrating the potential of this approach through a rigorous theoretical investigation and preliminary experimental exploration using simplified geometric constructs.

title: Quantum State Resonance Control and Modulation
abstract: Quantum state resonance control and modulation is a burgeoning field within quantum information science, offering unprecedented opportunities for manipulating and encoding quantum information. This paper explores the application of quantum state resonance control to achieve highly efficient quantum state manipulation. We propose a novel algorithm based on the non-linear properties of quantum states, specifically designed to precisely control the resonant frequencies and amplitudes of quantum systems. The core of this approach involves a self-adaptive resonance mechanism, allowing for dynamic optimization of the quantum state. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through simulations and preliminary experimental validation, revealing the potential for significant advancements in quantum information processing and encoding. The proposed approach represents a fundamental shift in how we approach quantum control, paving the way for new quantum information modalities.

title: 自适应量子拓扑的自适应变形 - 拓扑信息学算法的加速器
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithmic framework, termed "自适应量子拓扑的自适应变形", designed to accelerate the execution of various topological information processing algorithms. We propose a dynamic optimization strategy leveraging quantum topological properties to tailor the transformation process, offering a significant improvement over traditional approaches. The core mechanism centers around a self-tuning parameter set, which adjusts the algorithm's approach to the input data, leading to enhanced efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of numerical experiments on several prominent topological information processing tasks, showcasing substantial speedups compared to existing methods. This work represents a significant advancement in the field, offering a pathway toward more efficient and scalable topological information algorithms.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Computation Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed computation verification leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to establish a highly reliable verification chain between distributed computation nodes utilizing entanglement, effectively detecting and correcting errors that may arise during computation. Traditional distributed computation verification methods rely heavily on classical communication and data redundancy, often struggling with scalability and security. Our approach, however, utilizes entangled states to enable real-time state synchronization and error detection without requiring classical communication. This fundamentally changes the verification process, offering inherent resilience against errors even when individual nodes fail. The system relies on encoding computational results into quantum states and exploiting the correlations inherent in entangled states to identify and rectify discrepancies. The theoretical framework presented here demonstrates the potential for surpassing the limitations of classical computation in terms of fault tolerance and security. Key mathematical concepts including quantum state representation, entanglement quantification, and error detection protocols are outlined. The proposed method provides a pathway towards building robust and secure distributed computing systems suitable for demanding applications such as secure multi-party computation and large-scale scientific simulations. ---

title: 基于动态拓扑图的认知架构自适应优化
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cognitive architecture based on a dynamically adapting topology, termed a Neuro-Topological Network (NTN). The core claim is that cognitive architecture performance can be significantly improved by dynamically adjusting its internal topology to better accommodate evolving task demands and environmental changes, leading to more efficient cognitive processes. The NTN utilizes a reinforcement learning (RL) approach to optimize its topology in real-time. Nodes within the NTN represent cognitive modules (e.g., memory, reasoning, attention), while connection weights represent the interaction strength between these modules. The architecture adapts based on factors such as task difficulty, input complexity, and internal system activity. The optimization goals are to minimize task completion time, error rate, and resource consumption. The optimization strategies involve dynamic node addition/removal, weight adjustment, and routing strategy modifications. This approach contrasts with traditional static cognitive architectures and offers a more flexible and adaptive solution for complex cognitive tasks. The key contribution lies in applying reinforcement learning to the entire architecture topology, promoting holistic and efficient cognitive processes.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Simulation of Material Phase Transitions – Modeling Emergent Phenomena with Quantum Accuracy
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to simulating material phase transitions, leveraging the power of quantum mechanics to achieve unprecedented accuracy in modeling emergent phenomena. Traditional methods often struggle with the complex correlations inherent in these transitions, leading to inaccuracies and limitations in understanding the underlying physics. We introduce a quantum-enhanced simulation framework centered around quantum algorithms designed to accurately capture these subtle correlations, offering a significant advancement in the modeling of superconductivity, magnetism, and other complex phase transitions. The core mechanism involves simulating the evolution of the material's quantum state using quantum algorithms, while simultaneously incorporating a sophisticated correlation model to address the inherent difficulties of classical simulations. This paper details the design of the quantum simulation framework, explores its theoretical advantages, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its efficacy in simulating key phase transition scenarios.
